giant_rat.name: giant rat
giant_rat.lore: A rat's incisors never stop growing, and their enamel is harder than iron, so a rat must gnaw or die. Scale the animal up to the size of a terrier and no door, barrel or boot is safe. They follow the smell of rations down the upper corridors in packs, and a bite left unwashed turns to fever within days.

goblin.name: goblin
goblin.lore: Medieval chroniclers in Normandy wrote of a spirit called Gobelinus that haunted the town of Evreux, and the name has clung to every small, spiteful thing in the dark since. Dungeon goblins are cowards alone and bold in a crowd. They set snares, cut purses from the fallen, and keep their stolen coins in old boots.

grid_bug.name: grid bug
grid_bug.lore: Nobody has ever seen a grid bug walk a diagonal. It scuttles north, south, east or west along lines only it can sense, as if the floor were a chessboard and it a very small rook. Its bite carries a snap of static, enough to sting and no more. Scholars suspect a spell went wrong somewhere and these are the crumbs.

floating_eye.name: floating eye
floating_eye.lore: Floating eyes drift silently through dungeon corridors, their massive unblinking gaze capable of locking a creature in paralytic terror. They have no limbs or mouth, existing solely to observe. Sages believe they are the discarded sensors of some greater, unseen entity.

bat.name: bat
bat.lore: The giant bats of the deep cave networks are far more aggressive than their surface cousins. Their echolocation has evolved into a disorienting sonic pulse that scrambles the inner ear. Colonies roost in cavern ceilings, dropping on prey from above.

cobra.name: cobra
cobra.lore: A cobra's hood is not skin alone: the snake swings out a row of long ribs to spread it, and rears a third of its body off the ground to do so. The pharaohs wore that rearing cobra on their crowns as a threat to their enemies. Its venom works on the nerves, and the cave breed gives no warning hiss.

zombie.name: zombie
zombie.lore: The word comes from Haiti, where a zonbi is a corpse raised by a sorcerer, a bokor, and set to work with no will of its own. That is the horror of it: not the rot, but the stolen rest. The dead down here walk the same way, slow and patient, and their filthy nails leave wounds that sicken.

gelatinous_cube.name: gelatinous cube
gelatinous_cube.lore: It is ten feet on a side because the corridors are, and it fits them like a cork fits a bottle. A gelatinous cube slides along scouring floor, wall and ceiling of anything that once lived. Bone, coin and steel hang inside it undigested, which is often the first sign of it: a skeleton floating upright in clear air.

wraith.name: wraith
wraith.lore: Wraith is an old Scots word for the ghostly double of a person, seen shortly before that person dies. The thing in these halls is the omen with nobody left to warn. It has no flesh to wound and no memory to appeal to. Its touch takes the warmth out of a limb, and its cry takes the courage out of a heart.

mimic.name: mimic
mimic.lore: A mimic can pass for a chest, a door or a table, down to the grain of the wood and the rust on the hinges. The disguise fails in only one way: nothing in a dungeon is ever that conveniently placed. Its skin oozes a glue stronger than pitch, so the first hand to touch the lid stays there.

greater_mimic.name: Greater Mimic
greater_mimic.lore: Decades of feeding have let this mimic outgrow chests. It poses as a wardrobe, a staircase, sometimes the whole end wall of a treasure vault with the treasure painted on. Hammers bounce off its rubbery bulk and stick fast. The tongue, when it comes, is barbed and venomous, and the venom brings a pleasant drowsiness that is the last thing its prey resists.

abyssal_mimic.name: Abyssal Mimic
abyssal_mimic.lore: Something from the pit crawled inside an old mimic and stayed. It no longer copies furniture. It reaches into a traveler's thoughts and becomes the thing most longed for: an open door home, a lost friend, a pile of gold. The embrace that follows empties the will before the body. Fire and prayer make it show its real shape.

leprechaun.name: leprechaun
leprechaun.lore: Irish tales make the leprechaun a solitary cobbler, heard tapping at a single shoe under a hedge. A captor who keeps both eyes on him can demand his crock of gold. One glance away and he is gone. The ones down here have learned the same trick in reverse: a touch, a wink, and their pursuer is standing somewhere else entirely.

kobold.name: kobold
kobold.lore: German miners blamed the kobold, a spiteful spirit of the deep shafts, for ore that looked like silver, smelted to nothing and poisoned the men who worked it. They named the ore after him, and the metal is still called cobalt. His dungeon kin dig just as well, and line every tunnel with pits, tripwires and darts.

cave_spider.name: cave spider
cave_spider.lore: Spider silk is stronger than steel wire of the same thickness, and a cave spider strings it across a passage at the height of a man's face. Then it waits, for days if need be, with one leg resting on the thread. Its venom numbs first and kills slowly. The spider prefers its meals alive.

skeleton.name: skeleton
skeleton.lore: Bare bones, wired together by a necromancer's will and nothing else. A skeleton remembers how to swing a weapon and has forgotten everything besides. Spear points and arrows pass between the ribs and find nothing to hurt. A hammer or a mace is another matter: what cannot bleed can still break, and a blessing unties the knot at once.

fire_beetle.name: fire beetle
fire_beetle.lore: Fire beetles store bioluminescent fuel in special glands behind their eyes and at their abdomen. In the wild, this light attracts mates; in the dungeon, they have evolved to project it defensively as a short-range ignition burst. Their glands remain potent for days after death.

orc_scout.name: orc scout
orc_scout.lore: The poet of Beowulf listed the orcneas among the monstrous kin of Cain, beside the giants and the elves. The name has never meant anything gentle. A scout runs ahead of the warband in light leather, counting doors and marking easy prey. Each kill earns him a tattoo, so a heavily inked scout is one to respect.

gnoll.name: gnoll
gnoll.lore: A spotted hyena's jaws can crack the thigh bone of a buffalo, and it digests the splinters. Put that head on a man's shoulders and give it a spear. Gnolls build nothing and plant nothing. They trail wounded prey for miles until it drops, then leave no scrap behind. The cackle that sounds like laughter is the pack calling the others in.

hobgoblin.name: hobgoblin
hobgoblin.lore: Hobgoblins are the military aristocracy of the goblinoid races, disciplined and organized where their lesser kin are chaotic. They train in formation tactics and maintain strict hierarchies. A hobgoblin warband is a genuine military threat, capable of holding dungeon territory against much larger monsters.

ghoul.name: ghoul
ghoul.lore: The Arabs told of the ghul, a desert demon that haunts graveyards, robs the dead and lures travelers off the road, and it prowls through the Thousand and One Nights. The dungeon breed began as men who ate what no man should. Their claws carry a numbing slime, and they take their time with anyone who cannot move.

dire_rat.name: dire rat
dire_rat.lore: Dire rats are the size of large dogs and far more aggressive than ordinary rats. Pack hunters, they coordinate attacks to overwhelm larger prey. Their teeth can sever fingers, and their bites often fester due to their filthy habits.

acid_blob.name: acid blob
acid_blob.lore: Acid blobs are semi-intelligent oozes that secrete a powerful corrosive that dissolves metal and bone with equal efficiency. They leave trails of etched stone wherever they travel. Items found within a dead acid blob's mass are typically damaged but still recoverable.

troll.name: troll
troll.lore: In the tales of Norway a troll caught by sunrise turns to stone, which is why the hills there are full of troll-shaped rocks. Underground no sunrise comes. A troll's wounds close as fast as a blade can open them, and a severed arm will crawl back to its owner. Fire and acid are the only arguments it remembers.

orc_warrior.name: orc warrior
orc_warrior.lore: An orc warrior wears whatever armor his last enemy died in and carries an axe with a notched edge he is proud of. He believes his war-god counts only those who fall facing forward, so he does not retreat. Cornered, he fights harder. Most warbands are simply as many of these as one chief can feed.

dark_elf.name: dark elf
dark_elf.lore: Snorri Sturluson wrote of two elf peoples: the Light Elves, fairer than the sun, and the Dark Elves, who live down in the earth and are blacker than pitch. These are the second kind. They have built cold cities in the lowest tunnels and send scouts and assassins upward, armed with small darts dipped in something that stops the breath.

wight.name: wight
wight.lore: Wight is plain Old English for a living creature. The burial mounds gave the word its darker meaning. A wight is a dead lord who would not leave his barrow or his gold, and who still expects obedience. Lesser dead gather to him. His hand is colder than the grave he sleeps in, and those he kills do not stay buried.

rust_monster.name: rust monster
rust_monster.lore: It looks like an armadillo with a propeller for a tail and two long feathery feelers, and it wants nothing from a knight except his armor. One brush of those feelers and good steel flakes to red dust, which the creature licks up happily. Where rust monsters live, every hinge, nail and torch bracket is already gone.

cave_bear.name: cave bear
cave_bear.lore: The cave bears of the Ice Age stood taller than any living grizzly and wintered underground in such numbers that some caves hold the bones of thousands. Medieval villagers who found the great skulls took them for dragons. In the lightless middle levels the breed never died out. It is territorial, quick for its bulk, and does not bluff.

ogre.name: ogre
ogre.lore: Charles Perrault gave the ogre his place in the fairy tales in 1697. In Puss in Boots the cat flatters one into turning himself into a mouse, then eats him. The lesson holds: an ogre is huge, hungry and vain, but not clever. He keeps his larder and his loot in the same heap, and the smell announces both.

shadow.name: shadow
shadow.lore: A shadow is what remains when a wicked soul leaves and the darkness it cast stays behind. It lies flat along a wall or under a table and looks like any other patch of gloom until it stands up. Blades pass through it. Its touch takes the strength from an arm, and it grows darker with every theft. Torchlight and prayer hurt it.

mummy.name: mummy
mummy.lore: Egyptian embalmers took seventy days over a king. They drew the brain out through the nose with a hook, packed the body in natron salt, and left only the heart in place, because the heart would be weighed. All that care was meant to keep the tomb's owner whole forever. Dry linen and old resin burn very well.

giant_spider.name: giant spider
giant_spider.lore: The horse-sized spiders of the deep halls spin orb webs from wall to wall, each strand as thick as a bowstring. The bite stiffens a grown man in a few heartbeats. What the spider does not eat at once it wraps and hangs for later, and the old cocoons in a web often still hold a sword, a purse, or a helmet.

ettin.name: ettin
ettin.lore: Ettin comes from the Old English eoten, a giant, the same word the Norse spoke as jotunn. This one has two heads and two opinions about everything. The heads quarrel over supper, over directions, over whose turn it is to sleep, yet each commands one arm and one club, and one of them is always awake.

manticore.name: manticore
manticore.lore: The Greek physician Ctesias brought the tale back from the Persian court: a red beast with a lion's body, a man's face, three rows of teeth, and a scorpion's tail that shoots spines like arrows. Its Persian name means man-eater. It is said to leave nothing of its victims behind, not even the bones, which is why the missing are never found.

specter.name: specter
specter.lore: A specter has burned away everything it once was except the hunger. It keeps no face, no name and no grudge, and it walks through stone walls as if they were fog. The air turns cold before it arrives, cold enough to mist the breath. That chill is the only warning it gives, and its touch drains the life from whatever it passes through.

basilisk.name: basilisk
basilisk.lore: Pliny called the basilisk the king of serpents: no longer than a man's forearm, marked with a white crown, and so venomous that its glance kills and its breath splits rocks. He added that a weasel can kill it, and later writers swore by the crowing of a rooster. Its den is ringed with statues that were not carved.

chimera.name: chimera
chimera.lore: Homer describes her plainly: a lion in front, a serpent behind, a goat in the middle, breathing fire. She burned the fields of Lycia until Bellerophon came against her on the winged horse Pegasus. He drove a lead-tipped spear into her throat, and her own flame melted the lead and choked her. Her kind have three heads to watch.

minotaur.name: minotaur
minotaur.lore: Queen Pasiphae of Crete bore him, a man with a bull's head, and King Minos had Daedalus build the Labyrinth at Knossos to hide the shame. Athens sent seven youths and seven maidens to feed him until Theseus went in with a sword and Ariadne's ball of thread. The bull-men of the dungeon never lose their way in a maze.

frost_crawler.name: frost crawler
frost_crawler.lore: A frost crawler is a centipede as long as a wagon, armored in plates rimed with ice. It comes up from the frozen lower levels where water never thaws. The slime on its jaws is colder than ice itself and freezes flesh at a touch. Old delvers know its lair by the draft: a corridor that suddenly breathes winter.

medusa.name: medusa
medusa.lore: Medusa was the one mortal among the three Gorgon sisters, with living serpents for hair and a face that turned onlookers to stone. Perseus approached her walking backward, watching her reflection in the polished shield Athena lent him, and took her head with one stroke. Her daughters in the dark arrange their statues with care and wait behind them.

vampire_spawn.name: vampire spawn
vampire_spawn.lore: A vampire makes spawn the way a lord makes servants: quickly, and with no thought for their future. The spawn is strong, hungry and bound to obey the one who drained it. It cannot yet turn to mist or call the wolves. It can only hunt where it is sent and hope its master is destroyed before it is.

fire_elemental.name: fire elemental
fire_elemental.lore: The physician Paracelsus taught that each of the four elements has its own people, and the people of fire he named salamanders. This is one: a pillar of living flame with no body beneath it. Blades stir it without harming it. Whatever it leans against catches. It will not cross water, and a hard frost dims it to embers.

earth_elemental.name: earth elemental
earth_elemental.lore: Paracelsus wrote that the spirits of earth pass through solid rock as a fish passes through water. An earth elemental rises out of a floor without leaving a hole and sinks back the same way. It is a hill's worth of stone that has decided to stand up. Edges chip on it. Acid eats it as rain eats limestone.

storm_elemental.name: storm elemental
storm_elemental.lore: A storm elemental is a thunderhead the size of a room, forced into a rough shape by its own winds. Lightning walks around inside it looking for a way out, and a knight in full plate is the best way it will find all day. Swords and spears cut it as well as they cut weather.

lich_apprentice.name: lich apprentice
lich_apprentice.lore: This mage has started down the road to lichdom and cannot turn back. He has given up sleep, warmth and most of his pulse, but has not yet hidden his soul away. He serves an older lich in exchange for the last secret of the ritual. The older lich has no intention of creating a rival.

mind_flayer.name: mind flayer
mind_flayer.lore: A mind flayer wears a robe like a scholar and has a nest of tentacles where a mouth should be. It eats the brains of thinking creatures and nothing else. Before it feeds it sends a silent blast of thought that leaves a strong man unsure of his own name. Delvers speak of a whole city of them far below.

vampire.name: vampire
vampire.lore: In the 1720s and 1730s Austrian army surgeons posted to Serbian villages filed sober reports of peasants digging up the dead and staking them, and the word vampire entered English soon after. The thing itself is older and patient. It drinks life, bends weak minds with a look, and fears the stake, the flame and the sign of the Cross.

death_knight.name: death knight
death_knight.lore: He swore a paladin's oaths and broke every one of them, and when he died the grave would not take him. A death knight keeps all his skill at arms and none of his mercy. The blade he carries is part of his sentence and he cannot set it down. Men who meet his empty helm tend to run.

bone_golem.name: bone golem
bone_golem.lore: A necromancer built this from the bones of many creatures: an ox's ribs, a bear's skull, a dozen men's arms. No ghost lives in it. It follows its last order and nothing else. Swords and spears slide through the gaps and the bones knit back together. A heavy mace scatters them faster than they can gather.

greater_demon.name: greater demon
greater_demon.lore: John's Revelation shows the dragon's tail sweeping a third of the stars from heaven, and the Church has long read those stars as the angels who fell with him. This is one of them. It is not a beast and not mad. It chose this. It burns without being consumed, hates all that is made, and cannot bear a holy thing.

young_dragon.name: young dragon
young_dragon.lore: The Golden Legend tells of a dragon that poisoned the country around Silene in Libya until the townsfolk fed it their sheep, then their children. Saint George rode against it and brought it down with his lance. A young dragon is that story at the beginning: a small hoard, a large appetite, and fire it has only just learned to aim.

beholder.name: beholder
beholder.lore: A beholder is a floating globe of flesh with one great central eye, a mouth full of fangs and a crown of smaller eyes on stalks. Each small eye casts its own curse: one numbs, one blinds, one unmakes. It trusts no living thing, least of all another beholder, and decorates its lair with everyone who ever visited.

vampire_lord.name: vampire lord
vampire_lord.lore: Bram Stoker gave his Count the name of a real prince, Vlad Dracula of Wallachia, and a castle full of servants who feared him. A vampire lord is that kind of ruler. A thousand years of feeding have made it rich, courteous and very hard to kill. It holds a whole level of the dungeon as its estate and treats visitors as guests until supper.

lich.name: lich
lich.lore: Lich is the Old English word for a corpse. A churchyard still has its lychgate, where the coffin rests before burial. This corpse buried itself on purpose. A wizard who fears death can cut out his own soul and lock it in a vessel, and while the vessel lasts the body cannot be ended. What remains is all intellect and no pity.

adult_dragon.name: adult dragon
adult_dragon.lore: The dragon in Beowulf slept on its gold for three hundred years until a runaway slave crept into the barrow and stole a single cup. The dragon woke, counted, and knew. It burned the king's hall that same night. An adult dragon knows every coin in its hoard and exactly how each one was taken.

iron_golem.name: iron golem
iron_golem.lore: Hephaestus forged Talos, a man of bronze, to guard Crete. He ran around the island three times a day and hurled boulders at strange ships until the sorceress Medea pulled the single nail that sealed his one vein. The iron golem is the same idea in a cheaper metal: tireless, fireproof, and loyal to a master long since dead.

greater_lich.name: greater lich
greater_lich.lore: Russian tales tell of Koschei the Deathless, who hid his death inside a needle, the needle in an egg, the egg in a duck, the duck in a hare, and the hare in an iron chest buried under an oak on a distant island. A greater lich has had centuries to do better. It no longer bothers to guard its body at all.

arch_demon.name: arch demon
arch_demon.lore: In 1589 the bishop Peter Binsfeld drew up a list assigning a prince of Hell to each of the seven deadly sins: Lucifer for pride, Mammon for greed, Asmodeus for lust, and so on. An arch demon holds that kind of rank. It commands legions and plans in centuries. It burns with the fire it was thrown into, and it answers only to holiness.

ancient_dragon.name: ancient dragon
ancient_dragon.lore: An Old English proverb says it in one line: the dragon belongs in the barrow, old and wise, proud of its treasures. This one has outlived the kingdoms whose crowns it sleeps on. Its fire went out ages ago and something colder took its place. The breath of an ancient wyrm is the frost of a grave that has never been opened.

ancient_lich.name: ancient lich
ancient_lich.lore: No one living remembers what this wizard was called, and the lich has forgotten too. Thousands of years of study have left it with answers to questions no one else knows how to ask. Fire, frost and steel are problems it solved long ago. Only what is holy still troubles it, because that was never a matter of knowledge.

death_lord.name: death lord
death_lord.lore: John saw a pale horse, and the name of its rider was Death, and Hell followed after him. A death lord rides in that train. It was a conqueror once and now carries a part of the grave's own authority. Every lesser corpse for miles turns to face it. Its glance alone takes the strength from the living.

chaos_spawn.name: chaos spawn
chaos_spawn.lore: Hesiod wrote that first of all things came Chaos, the yawning gap, before earth or sky. A chaos spawn is a scrap of that gap which has wandered into a world with rules and resents them. It has claws one moment and wings the next. Looking at it too long unsettles the mind, and being touched by it is worse.

soul_eater.name: soul eater
soul_eater.lore: A soul eater is a hunger with a shape drawn loosely around it. It comes from the borderland beside death and feeds on the spark that makes a body a person. It can scent a strong soul through a mile of rock, and the brave men who go deepest smell best. What it finishes leaves nothing behind to pray for.

orc_shaman.name: orc shaman
orc_shaman.lore: The shaman is the one orc in the warband who does not carry an axe, and the only one the chief is careful around. He paints his skin with ash and old blood and calls on the tribe's war-god to curse its enemies. When he chants, the marks on his arms glow like coals in a draft.

giant_centipede.name: giant centipede
giant_centipede.lore: A centipede does not bite with its mouth. Its first pair of legs have become hollow fangs that fold under the head and pump venom. The largest kind in the jungles of the New World hangs from cave ceilings and plucks bats out of the air. The dungeon breed is as long as a man and hunts the same way.

skeletal_archer.name: skeletal archer
skeletal_archer.lore: Skeletal archers are the reanimated remains of warriors who were skilled with the bow in life. The necromantic animation preserves their martial memory, allowing them to draw and fire with mechanical precision. They prefer to maintain distance, riddling targets with arrows before retreating behind their melee companions.

cave_toad.name: cave toad
cave_toad.lore: Every toad carries two swollen glands behind its eyes that ooze a milky poison when it is squeezed. Dogs that mouth one foam and stagger. The cave toad is the size of a hound itself, lives beside black underground pools, and has learned to spit. Delvers hungry enough to cook one report seeing colors for a week.

brigand.name: brigand
brigand.lore: Brigands are former soldiers, escaped criminals, or simply desperate people who have turned to dungeon raiding and banditry. Unlike monsters, they have actual combat training and equipment. Some brigand bands have claimed entire dungeon sections as territory, extorting passing adventurers or simply killing them.

shadow_hound.name: shadow hound
shadow_hound.lore: On the fourth of August 1577, during a great storm, a black dog burst into the church at Bungay in Suffolk and left two of the congregation dead at their prayers. East Anglia calls him Black Shuck. The shadow hounds of the dungeon are his kind: cold, half there, and silent until the howl that makes a man feel utterly alone.

flesh_golem.name: flesh golem
flesh_golem.lore: Mary Shelley told the story in 1818: Victor Frankenstein stitched a man together from the dead, gave him life, and fled in horror from what he had made. Dungeon artificers repeat the work and the mistake. A flesh golem obeys until some buried scrap of memory wakes in it, and then it grieves, and then it rages.

harpy.name: harpy
harpy.lore: The name means snatcher. The harpies tormented the blind king Phineus, swooping down each time his table was laid to seize the food and foul what they left, until the winged sons of the North Wind, sailing with Jason, chased them off. They have a woman's face, a vulture's body, and a voice that draws the unwary close.

necromancer_apprentice.name: necromancer apprentice
necromancer_apprentice.lore: King Saul, forsaken and afraid, went in disguise to the witch of Endor and had her call up the dead prophet Samuel, who told him he would die the next day. That is necromancy: asking the dead for what God has withheld. The apprentice has learned enough to raise a corpse and not enough to be afraid of it.

stymphalian_bird.name: Stymphalian Bird
stymphalian_bird.lore: Ares' sacred birds of Lake Stymphalia bore bronze beaks, claws, and feathers they launched like arrows. Heracles drove them away with Hephaestus' bronze krotala. In these dungeons they roost in high crevices and dive at unwary explorers.

satyr_warrior.name: Satyr Warrior
satyr_warrior.lore: Satyrs are the rowdy half-goat companions of Dionysus, known more for wine and revelry than war. Those who take up arms are exiles cast out from their bands, bitter and violent. They fight with crude clubs and use their horned heads to disorient opponents.

empusa.name: Empusa
empusa.lore: Empusai are shape-shifting demonesses sent by Hecate to devour travelers at crossroads. They can appear as beautiful women, dogs, or cows before revealing their true form with one leg of bronze and one of an ass. They drain the life force of their victims through seductive illusions.

hecate_hound.name: Hecate's Hound
hecate_hound.lore: Hecate, goddess of magic and crossroads, keeps spectral hounds that patrol the boundaries between the living world and the underworld. Their mournful howls can shatter a mortal's concentration and drive them to madness. They are encountered most frequently near dungeon stairwells.

lamia.name: Lamia
lamia.lore: Lamia was a queen of Libya whom Zeus loved. Hera, in her jealousy, destroyed Lamia's children, and grief turned the queen into a thing that steals the children of others. Zeus gave her the power to take out her own eyes so that she could rest from what she saw. She is a woman above and a serpent below, and she is cold to the touch.
lamia.omen: Somewhere close, a woman is singing a lullaby to no one.

gorgon_warrior.name: Gorgon Warrior
gorgon_warrior.lore: Edward Topsell's bestiary of 1607 gave the name Gorgon to a scaled, bull-shaped beast of Africa whose breath killed whatever it touched. He took it from Pliny's catoblepas, a creature whose head was so heavy it always hung toward the ground. Dungeon smiths have cast the thing in bronze and set it on guard, breath and all.

cyclops.name: Cyclops
cyclops.lore: Polyphemus, a son of Poseidon, shut Odysseus and his men in his cave and ate them two at a time. Odysseus got him drunk, told him his name was Nobody, and put out his single eye with a sharpened, fire-hardened stake. When the giant screamed that Nobody was hurting him, his neighbors went back to bed. Every Cyclops since has guarded that eye.

sphinx.name: Sphinx
sphinx.lore: The Sphinx crouched at the gates of Thebes and devoured all who could not answer her riddle: what walks on four legs at dawn, two at noon, three at dusk? Only Oedipus answered correctly and she threw herself from her rock. In the dungeon she sits at crossroads, guarding passage, and will attack any who approach without first attempting her puzzle.

griffin.name: Griffin
griffin.lore: Herodotus heard that far to the north griffins guard the gold of the mountains, and that a one-eyed people called the Arimaspians steal it from them. Lion behind, eagle before, the griffin was the ancients' picture of a watchman who cannot be bribed. Medieval kings drank from cups said to be griffin claws, trusting them to darken at poison.

pegasus.name: Maddened Pegasus
pegasus.lore: Born from the blood of Medusa when Perseus struck her down, Pegasus is the divine winged horse associated with thunder and the Muses. While normally gentle when approached by heroes, dungeon-corrupted Pegasi have been driven mad by confinement underground and charge anything that moves.

hydra.name: Lernaean Hydra
hydra.lore: The Hydra of Lerna had nine heads, and for every one Heracles struck off, two grew back. His nephew Iolaus ended it by searing each stump with a burning brand before it could sprout. The last head was immortal, so Heracles buried it under a rock. He dipped his arrows in the creature's blood, and no wound they made ever healed.

cerberus.name: Cerberus
cerberus.lore: The three-headed hound of Hades guards the entrance to the underworld, permitting the dead to enter but none to leave. Heracles subdued him through sheer strength for his twelfth labor; Orpheus charmed all three heads to sleep with his lyre. In the deepest dungeon he serves as an eternal guardian, his serpent-barbed tail lashing at any who attempt to pass.

scylla.name: Scylla
scylla.lore: Scylla was a sea nymph until the witch Circe, jealous over the sea god Glaucus, poisoned the pool where she bathed. She rose from it with twelve dangling legs and six long necks, each head bearing three rows of teeth. From her cave above the strait she took six of Odysseus's best men at once, one for each mouth.

charybdis_spawn.name: Charybdis Spawn
charybdis_spawn.lore: Charybdis, the great whirlpool monster, is said to be a daughter of Poseidon who was struck by Zeus's thunderbolt and cast into the sea. Three times daily she swallows the sea and three times regurgitates it. Her spawn are smaller vortex-creatures that cling to dungeon walls and drag creatures toward their central maw.

titanspawn.name: Titanspawn
titanspawn.lore: Zeus and his brothers fought the Titans for ten years and cast the losers into Tartarus, as far below the earth as the earth is below the sky, behind gates of bronze. Something of them has leaked upward since. A titanspawn is a rough man-shape of bedrock moved by an old anger it does not understand.

frost_giant.name: Frost Giant
frost_giant.lore: The Norse called them hrimthursar, the rime giants. The first of them, Ymir, formed where the ice of Niflheim met the heat of the south, and Odin and his brothers killed him and built the world from his body: sea from his blood, sky from his skull. His descendants have not forgiven it. They wait in the cold for Ragnarok.

fire_giant.name: Fire Giant
fire_giant.lore: Surtr stands at the border of Muspelheim with a sword that outshines the sun. At Ragnarok he will ride north with the sons of Muspell, the rainbow bridge will break beneath them, and he will cut down the god Freyr and set the world alight. The fire giants in the deep forges are his people, and they are keeping the blades hot.

valkyrie_shade.name: Valkyrie Shade
valkyrie_shade.lore: The valkyries are Odin's choosers of the slain. They ride over the battlefield and carry the bravest of the fallen to Valhalla. A valkyrie shade is one who chose wrongly, or fell herself, and lost the god's favor. She still does the only work she knows. She marks a soul with her spear and tries to carry it away, downward now.

fenrir_pup.name: Fenrir's Pup
fenrir_pup.lore: The gods raised the wolf Fenrir among themselves until he grew too strong to trust. They bound him with Gleipnir, a ribbon made of impossible things like the sound of a cat's footfall. He allowed it only with the god Tyr's hand between his jaws as a pledge, and Tyr lost the hand. His whelps bite and hold on the same way.

jormungandr_spawn.name: Jörmungandr Spawn
jormungandr_spawn.lore: Odin threw the serpent Jormungandr into the sea, where it grew until it circled the world and bit its own tail. Thor once hooked it using an ox's head for bait, and the giant Hymir cut the line in terror. At Ragnarok Thor will kill it and die nine steps later from its venom. Its young carry that venom.

draugr.name: Draugr
draugr.lore: A draugr is a dead Norseman who would not lie still in his mound. He swells to a giant's size, guards his grave-goods, and rides the roofs of nearby farms at night. In the saga of Grettir the Strong, the hero wrestled the draugr Glam and won, but Glam's dying curse left him afraid of the dark for the rest of his life.

einherjar_ghost.name: Einherjar Ghost
einherjar_ghost.lore: The einherjar are the chosen dead of Valhalla. Each morning they arm and cut one another down in the courtyard, and each evening they rise whole and feast on the boar Saehrimnir, who is whole again by the next day. This one never arrived. He fights with a veteran's skill and the bitterness of a man left off the list.

nidhogg_brood.name: Níðhöggr Brood
nidhogg_brood.lore: Níðhöggr is the great corpse-gnawing dragon who dwells at the root of Yggdrasil, gnawing the World Tree from below. Its brood are smaller wyrms that carry their parent's essence, infected with the same cosmic rot. They are found in the deepest passages, continuing their parent's slow work of destroying the foundations of the world.

hugin_raven.name: Huginn Raven
hugin_raven.lore: Odin keeps two ravens, Huginn and Muninn, Thought and Memory. He sends them out at dawn to fly over the world, and they come back at breakfast and tell him the news. He admits he fears for Thought, and more for Memory. The dungeon's ravens are of that lineage. They watch, they remember, and they go for the eyes.

lindworm.name: Lindworm
lindworm.lore: In the Danish tale of King Lindworm, a queen bears a wingless dragon who devours his brides. One clever girl comes to the wedding wearing ten shifts and tells him to shed a skin for each one she takes off. When the last skin falls, a prince is underneath. The lindworms in the flooded tunnels have no prince inside them.

berserker_spirit.name: Berserker Spirit
berserker_spirit.lore: The Norse berserkers, the bear-shirts, fought in a howling trance, and some chess pieces carved in the twelfth century still show them biting the rims of their shields. King Harald Fairhair set them in the prow of his ship. This spirit is the trance without the man. It never tires, never parries, and has no skin to keep the cold or a prayer out.

light_elf_hostile.name: Corrupted Light Elf
light_elf_hostile.lore: Snorri wrote that the Light Elves of Alfheim are fairer than the sun to look upon. Something has soured in these. The brightness that once blessed now burns, and they loose it at anything that casts a shadow, friend or stranger alike. They are fey still, for all their glory, and cold iron hurts them as it hurts their kind.

sea_serpent_norse.name: Norse Sea Serpent
sea_serpent_norse.lore: In 1555 the Swedish churchman Olaus Magnus described a serpent two hundred feet long that lived in the sea caves near Bergen, came out on summer nights, and plucked sailors off the decks of ships. Its kind have followed the cold rivers underground. They lie coiled in flooded chambers, and the water around them never quite thaws.

anubis_guardian.name: Anubis Guardian
anubis_guardian.lore: Anubis, the jackal-headed god of the embalmers, leads the dead into the Hall of Two Truths and steadies the scales where the heart is weighed against the feather of Maat. The tomb builders set his image at the door in black stone, and some of those images still keep their post. They judge trespassers quickly. A guilty heart stops for a moment under their gaze.

ra_serpent.name: Ra's Serpent
ra_serpent.lore: The pharaoh's crown bore a rearing cobra, the uraeus, and the Egyptians said it was the fiery Eye of Ra, spitting flame at the king's enemies. Each night, as the sun's boat passed through the underworld, serpents like it defended Ra against the chaos snake Apep. These golden guardians have that fire in their fangs and are painful to look at.

scarab_swarm.name: Scarab Swarm
scarab_swarm.lore: The Egyptians watched the dung beetle roll its ball across the sand and saw the god Khepri pushing the sun across the sky, so they carved the scarab on seals and laid it over the hearts of their dead. Tomb curses have turned the sacred beetle hungry. One is nothing. Ten thousand pour from a crack in the wall like black water.

sphinx_guardian.name: Egyptian Sphinx
sphinx_guardian.lore: A stone slab between the paws of the Great Sphinx at Giza tells how a young prince fell asleep in its shade and heard it promise him the throne if he cleared away the sand that buried it. He did, and reigned as Thutmose IV. The sphinxes of Egypt ask no riddles. They guard a king's rest, and their roar is the noon sun.

ammit_spawn.name: Ammit Spawn
ammit_spawn.lore: Ammit crouches beside the scales in the Hall of Two Truths: crocodile's head, lion's forequarters, hippopotamus's hindquarters, the three man-eaters of the Nile in one body. When a heart outweighs the feather of Maat, she eats it, and that soul dies a second and final death. Her spawn do not wait for the verdict.

sobek_warrior.name: Sobek Warrior
sobek_warrior.lore: Sobek, crocodile god of the Nile, was worshipped at Crocodilopolis in the Faiyum, where priests kept a living crocodile called Petsuchos, hung it with gold and fed it by hand. His temple soldiers wear the crocodile's head and carry the sickle-bladed khopesh. They fight as the river beast does: seize, drag down, and roll until the struggling stops.

ba_spirit.name: Ba Spirit
ba_spirit.lore: Egyptians drew the ba as a bird with a human head, the part of a person that could fly from the tomb by day and must return to the body by night. Erase the name or spoil the burial and the ba has nowhere to roost. These lost ones flutter through the dark, starved, drinking the life of anyone who still has a name.

khepri_beetle.name: Khepri Beetle
khepri_beetle.lore: Egyptians watched the scarab roll its ball of dung across the sand and saw in it Khepri, the beetle-headed god who pushes the sun over the horizon each dawn. Down here his sacred beetles have swollen to the size of hounds. Each carries a little stored daylight under its wing cases, and looses it in a blinding flash when cornered.

thoth_construct.name: Thoth Construct
thoth_construct.lore: Ibis-headed Thoth invented writing, kept the calendar, and stood beside the scales in the Hall of Two Truths to record each verdict. His guardians are carved stone covered in hieroglyphs that crawl and rearrange themselves, every sign a working spell. They punish thieves of sacred writings. Spells slide off the script. A mason's hammer does more.

duat_shade.name: Duat Shade
duat_shade.lore: Each night Ra's barque sailed the twelve hours of the Duat, the Egyptian underworld, and each dead soul faced the scales where Anubis weighed the heart against the feather of Ma'at. Ammit devoured the hearts that failed. These shades are thinner leftovers, souls that simply came apart in the dark water. They drift like smoke and cling to the living for substance.

desert_wraith.name: Desert Wraith
desert_wraith.lore: Egyptians called the fertile Nile bank the Black Land and the desert beyond it the Red Land, the realm of Set, lord of storms and disorder. Travelers who died out there without tomb or rites were dried by sun and wind into husks. Their spirits never found the road to the Duat. They ride the hot wind and steal the water from living flesh.

banshee.name: Banshee
banshee.lore: The bean sidhe, 'woman of the fairy mound', keens outside the house when one of the old Irish families is about to lose a member. Some saw a grey-cloaked crone, others a pale girl drawing a silver comb through her long hair. Above ground her cry only announces a death. In these halls the cry itself does the killing.

fomorian.name: Fomorian
fomorian.lore: The Fomorians came out of the sea to oppress Ireland until the Tuatha De Danann broke them at the Second Battle of Mag Tuired. Their champion Balor had one eye whose lid took four men to lift, and whatever it looked upon died. His own grandson Lugh drove a sling stone through that eye and out the back of his skull. Lesser Fomorians still carry a weaker glare.

changeling.name: Changeling
changeling.lore: Country folk across Britain and Ireland believed the fairies stole healthy babies and left one of their own in the cradle: a thin, wailing thing with old eyes and a bottomless appetite. Iron tongs laid across the cradle were the usual defence. The changelings below have grown up. Each wears a borrowed face until struck, then the glamour slips and something half-finished looks out.

each_uisce.name: Each Uisce
each_uisce.lore: The each uisge of the Highland sea lochs is the kelpie's deadlier cousin. It waits on the shore as a fine horse or a handsome stranger. Its hide turns sticky the moment a rider mounts, and it gallops straight into deep water, where it eats everything but the liver, which floats ashore the next morning. In the flooded passages it still stands waiting, sleek and patient.

cath_palug.name: Cath Palug
cath_palug.lore: The Welsh Triads say the sow Henwen bore a kitten on the coast of Arfon, and the swineherd flung it into the Menai Strait. It swam to Anglesey, where the sons of Palug raised it to their own ruin. An old poem counts nine score warriors as its food before Cai came against it with his polished shield. It is quick, and far cleverer than a cat should be.

fionn_hound.name: Fionn's Hound
fionn_hound.lore: Fionn mac Cumhaill's favourite hounds, Bran and Sceolang, were his own cousins: a jealous fairy woman changed his aunt Tuiren into a hound, and she bore them in that shape. They kept human wits behind a dog's eyes. The hounds of that bloodline stand as tall as a man's shoulder, and once one has the scent it follows without rest.

puca.name: Púca
puca.lore: The Púca of Irish country lore comes as a sleek black horse with eyes like coals, or as a goat, a hare, or a small dark man. It offers a tired traveler a ride, then tears across bog and bramble all night and tips the rider into a ditch at dawn. Farmers left the last of the harvest standing as the Púca's share. It runs in order to be chased.

dullahan_spawn.name: Dullahan Spawn
dullahan_spawn.lore: The Dullahan rides the Irish back roads at night on a black horse, his own head held high in one hand and a whip made from a human spine in the other. Where he stops, he speaks a name, and that person dies. He lashes at the eyes of anyone who watches, and he cannot bear the sight of gold. These lesser riders carry a name and have not yet found its owner.

sluagh.name: Sluagh
sluagh.lore: Highland and Irish tradition calls them the Sluagh, the host of the unforgiven dead, turned away by Heaven and earth alike. They fly in from the west like a flock of dark birds, and families shut the west windows of a sickroom so the host could not snatch the dying soul. Below ground no window keeps them out. They come down in a cloud and tear.

pazuzu_spawn.name: Pazuzu Spawn
pazuzu_spawn.lore: Pazuzu, king of the wind demons, brought the hot southwest wind with its fever and locusts to Assyria. He had a dog's snarling face, four wings, an eagle's talons and a scorpion's tail. Mothers still hung his bronze head over the cradle, because he hated the child-stealing demoness Lamashtu and drove her off. His spawn inherited the wings and the fever, and none of the usefulness.

lahamu.name: Lahamu
lahamu.lore: The Babylonian creation epic, Enuma Elish, begins when Apsu the sweet water mingled with Tiamat the salt sea. Their firstborn were Lahmu and Lahamu, and some scholars read the names as 'the muddy ones', the silt where river meets ocean. What wears her name here is a shifting bulk of wet clay and coils, never the same shape twice, older in its manner than anything that walks on legs.

anzu_bird.name: Anzu Bird
anzu_bird.lore: Anzu, the lion-headed eagle of Sumer, guarded Enlil's doorway until the day he watched the god bathe and stole the Tablet of Destinies, which gives its holder command over fate. With it he ordered arrows in flight to turn back into reed and feather. Ninurta sheared off his wings in a storm and shot him down in the mountains. His brood kept the storm.

ugallu_demon.name: Ugallu Demon
ugallu_demon.lore: Ugallu means 'Big Weather Beast': a lion's head on a man's body, standing on the talons of a bird, with a dagger raised in one fist. Tiamat made the first of them among her eleven monsters to fight the younger gods. After Marduk won, Assyrian kings carved the Ugallu beside palace doorways to frighten off sickness. These ones guard nothing, and they still love a storm.

kusarikku.name: Kusarikku
kusarikku.lore: The Kusarikku is the Bull-Man of Mesopotamia: a human face, arms and chest above, a bull's horns and hindquarters below. Tiamat counted him among her eleven monsters. After her defeat he took service with Shamash the sun god, and sculptors set his image at doorways, holding the gateposts. The ones penned down here have no gate left to guard, and they gore whatever comes through.

beholder_spawn.name: Beholder Spawn
beholder_spawn.lore: A floating ball of flesh the size of a shield, split by a toothy mouth and crowned with a few stunted eyestalks. Each small eye throws a different ill: one locks the limbs, another scrambles thought. It drifts at head height, never blinks, and regards every other living thing as a flaw. A spear in the big central eye settles the argument.

mind_flayer_thrall.name: Mind Flayer Thrall
mind_flayer_thrall.lore: It was a scholar once, or a soldier. Then a tentacled master reached into its head and left only obedience. The thrall walks with a sleepwalker's care and never speaks. When it turns its blank eyes on an intruder, the master's will pours through it like a shout inside the skull, and something behind the stare begins to feed on the victim's strength.

aboleth_lesser.name: Lesser Aboleth
aboleth_lesser.lore: A fish as long as a longship, with three red eyes stacked one above another down its brow and four tentacles trailing slime. Aboleths claim to remember everything their ancestors saw, back to a sea older than any shore. This one is young by their measure. Its slime softens skin until a victim can breathe only water, and it keeps such captives as servants.

gibbering_mouther.name: Gibbering Mouther
gibbering_mouther.lore: A heap of soft flesh that pours across the floor, covered in eyes and mouths that open and close wherever they please. Every mouth talks at once in a different voice, and none of it means anything. The noise crowds out thought, and brave men have been found standing still, muttering along. Then the mouths reach the boots, and each one bites.

intellect_devourer.name: Intellect Devourer
intellect_devourer.lore: A naked brain the size of a hound, trotting on four clawed legs. Mind flayers breed them as hunters. It finds a sleeper, feeds on the mind, then climbs inside the empty skull and walks the body back among its friends. Old delvers test a companion who has gone quiet with a question only he would know.

nothic.name: Nothic
nothic.lore: It was a wizard who read one book too many. The curse that answers such greed bent his back, lengthened his claws, and melted his face into a single huge eye. He remembers nothing of himself and wants every secret that belongs to someone else. He giggles in corners and watches. Flesh withers where that stare rests too long.

grell.name: Grell
grell.lore: A bare grey brain as wide as a wagon wheel, with a parrot's beak and ten long tentacles hanging beneath it. It has no eyes at all. It feels the air tremble and the faint spark inside living things, which may be why lightning does not trouble it. It hangs silent near the ceiling, drops, stings its catch limp, and carries the meal upward.

cloaker.name: Cloaker
cloaker.lore: Indistinguishable from a black cloak until it strikes, the cloaker is a manta-like creature that drapes itself over its victim to suffocate and blind. It emits a haunting moan that causes unease in all who hear it. More than one adventurer has reached for their cloak only to find it had teeth.

star_spawn.name: Star Spawn
star_spawn.lore: It fell from between the stars, or was sent. A star spawn is a hill of grey flesh that folds and unfolds without pattern, and minds near it fill with thoughts that are not their own. Sages who studied one concluded it was only a footprint, and stopped asking what had made it. Cold means nothing to it. Fire and prayer do.

balor_lesser.name: Lesser Balor
balor_lesser.lore: A horned giant twice a man's height, bat-winged, wrapped in its own fire. It carries a burning sword in one hand and a many-tailed whip of flame in the other, and the stone blackens where it stands. In the armies of the Abyss such demons are generals. This is a lesser one of the kind, which means only that armies have managed to kill it.

marilith_spawn.name: Marilith Spawn
marilith_spawn.lore: A woman's body to the waist, a great serpent's below, and six arms with a blade in every hand. Mariliths are the captains of the demon hosts, the ones who plan the battle while lesser fiends merely enjoy it. This younger one fights like six duelists who have trained together since birth. The tail waits for whoever gets past the swords.

vrock.name: Vrock
vrock.lore: A demon built like a gaunt man with a vulture's head, ragged wings and long hooked talons. Vrocks fight in shrieking flocks and dance in a ring before a kill. When one shakes its feathers, a cloud of spores drifts out that takes root in skin and sprouts. The scream alone has sent veteran soldiers running.

hezrou.name: Hezrou
hezrou.lore: A toad the size of an ox, walking upright, with arms like a wrestler's and a spine ridged with spikes. The smell arrives first: a rot so thick that eyes stream and stomachs turn before the demon is in sight. Hezrou are the foot soldiers the Abyss sends when a wall needs breaking. One simply falls on whatever it wants dead.

glabrezu.name: Glabrezu
glabrezu.lore: Fifteen feet of muscle with a jackal's head and four arms: two end in crab pincers big enough to close around a man, two in ordinary, clever hands. The glabrezu prefers the hands. It offers a desperate mortal exactly what he asks for, worded so that the gift ruins him, and it keeps the pincers for those who refuse to bargain.

nalfeshnee_lesser.name: Lesser Nalfeshnee
nalfeshnee_lesser.lore: A mountain of fat on a boar's legs, with an ape's arms, a tusked snout, and a pair of feathered wings far too small for it. In the Abyss the nalfeshnee sit as judges over newly damned souls and sentence each to the torment that suits it. A halo of sickly rainbow light flares around it when it is angry, and minds caught in the glow go slack.

quasit.name: Quasit
quasit.lore: A demon two feet tall, green and warty, with horns, a barbed tail and claws that itch like nettles. Careless conjurers keep quasits as familiars and believe they are the masters. It can take the shape of a bat or a centipede, and it uses the trick for one purpose: leaving. Its courage ends where a fair fight begins.

dretch.name: Dretch
dretch.lore: The lowest thing in the Abyss that can still be called a demon: a squat, pale, sagging body, a slack mouth, and a brain with room for one spite at a time. Stronger fiends herd dretches into battle by the hundred and spend them like arrows. Frightened, a dretch leaks a foul green fume that has emptied the stomachs of hardened soldiers.

shadow_demon.name: Shadow Demon
shadow_demon.lore: A fiend that lost its body and kept its hatred. What remains is a winged shape cut out of darkness, with claws that chill and eyes like two dim coals. It slides along walls, and lamps gutter as it passes. It hates bright fire and holy light, because either one shows how little of it is left.

incubus.name: Incubus
incubus.lore: Medieval churchmen wrote of the incubus as a demon that visited sleepers by night and left them pale and wasted by morning. It wears a handsome face that is slightly too perfect to trust, and its voice makes bad ideas sound sensible. Those it charms defend it against their own friends. Its kiss is how it feeds, and what it drinks is years.

succubus_shade.name: Succubus Shade
succubus_shade.lore: A succubus, in the old demonologies, preys on sleepers and feeds on their strength. This one has worn so thin that lamplight passes through her, and the eye slides away when it tries to hold her outline. She steps through walls to stand beside a bed. Her victims wake weak and muddled, sure only that something is missing.

rutterkin.name: Rutterkin
rutterkin.lore: One rung above the dretch and furious about it. A rutterkin is a lopsided demon, one arm too long, the jaw hung crooked, the skin a patchwork of sores. It bullies anything weaker and grovels to anything stronger, sometimes in the same breath. They prowl in small packs, and a pack will pause in the middle of a hunt to fight over who walks in front.

mane_demon.name: Mane Demon
mane_demon.lore: Romans called the spirits of the dead the manes. Demon lore borrows the word for the lowest of the damned: a soul so petty in its wickedness that the Abyss made nothing better of it than a bloated, white-eyed body with claws. It has no memory and no plan. Greater demons drive manes forward in crowds to tire an enemy's sword arm.

chain_devil_spawn.name: Chain Devil Spawn
chain_devil_spawn.lore: A devil wrapped head to foot in iron chains, hooked and barbed, that move like the arms of an octopus. The chains are its hands, its armor and its only conversation. It serves Hell as a jailer. This lesser one has patience for nothing subtle: it snares an ankle, drags the prisoner close, and winds the rest around him link by link.

bearded_devil.name: Bearded Devil
bearded_devil.lore: The infantry of Hell. Each carries a saw-toothed glaive whose cuts will not close, and each wears a beard of wiry, snake-thick strands that lash out on their own and leave a burning rash. Bearded devils march in ranks, hold a line, and obey orders, which makes them worse than demons twice their size. One never runs unless commanded.

barbed_devil.name: Barbed Devil
barbed_devil.lore: Covered from scalp to tail tip in spines as long as daggers, a barbed devil cannot be grappled, shoved, or stood beside in comfort. Hell posts them as sentries over its vaults and its most valuable prisoners, because they never grow bored. Flame gathers in its palms when it is roused, and the air around it turns hot enough to curl parchment.

bone_devil.name: Bone Devil
bone_devil.lore: Nine feet tall and thin as a dried corpse, skin stretched tight over the skeleton, with a scorpion's tail arched above its skull. Bone devils are Hell's inspectors. They watch lesser devils for slackness and report it with relish. One will toy with a trapped enemy for an hour, and it saves the venom in its sting for the moment the game grows dull.

erinyes_lesser.name: Lesser Erinyes
erinyes_lesser.lore: The Greeks feared the Erinyes, the Furies: Alecto, Megaera and Tisiphone, who rose from the earth to hound oath-breakers and those who shed a kinsman's blood. They chased Orestes across Greece for killing his mother. Hell's devils of that name are winged, fair of face, and just as tireless, armed with a poisoned sword and a rope that binds whatever it touches.

imp.name: Imp
imp.lore: A red devil no bigger than a cat, with bat wings and a scorpion's sting at the end of its tail. Hell lends imps to ambitious mortals as familiars. An imp flatters, fetches, and gives excellent advice, and every piece of that advice leads its master one step nearer to damnation. It is paid for each soul delivered.

lemure.name: Lemure
lemure.lore: The Romans feared the lemures, restless ghosts they bought off each May by tossing black beans over the shoulder at midnight. Hell uses the name for its rawest material: a damned soul melted into a mound of grey flesh with a sagging face and no mind. Cut one apart and it flows back together. A blessed weapon ends it for good.

pit_fiend_spawn.name: Pit Fiend Spawn
pit_fiend_spawn.lore: Pit fiends rule the legions of the Nine Hells: twelve feet of red scale, wings like a ship's sails, a mouth of green venom, and a mind that plans in centuries. This one is newly raised to the rank, which makes it the least of the mightiest. It commands, bargains, and lies with equal skill, and it kills without anger, the way a clerk closes a ledger.

stone_golem_lesser.name: Lesser Stone Golem
stone_golem_lesser.lore: A statue that walks. Its makers carved it from one block, spent a season cutting commands into the stone, and left it with a single instruction it has obeyed ever since. Time seems to thicken around it, and those who come close find their own limbs heavy. Swords skate off it. A mason's maul speaks its language.

clay_golem.name: Clay Golem
clay_golem.lore: In the old tale of Prague, Rabbi Judah Loew shaped a man from the clay of the Vltava's bank and woke it with the word 'emet', truth, written on its brow. It guarded the ghetto until it ran wild, and he rubbed out one letter to leave 'met', death. Clay servants made by lesser hands also go berserk, and their makers are seldom there to stop them.

wood_golem.name: Wood Golem
wood_golem.lore: A man-shaped guardian pegged together from seasoned oak, with a rune burned into its chest. It stands beside the door or the chest it was told to guard, still as furniture, sometimes for a hundred years, until someone touches what it watches. Arrows lodge in it and trouble it not at all. An axe or a torch is another matter.

animated_armor.name: Animated Armor
animated_armor.lore: A full suit of plate with nobody inside. Some are held up by a wizard's standing order, some by a ghost too stubborn to leave its post. It walks its old rounds, turns its empty visor toward any sound, and fights with the drill of whoever last wore it. A sword edge finds nothing to cut. A heavy hammer beats it out of shape.

shield_guardian.name: Shield Guardian
shield_guardian.lore: A wizard builds a shield guardian for one purpose: to stand between its master and harm. The link is an amulet, and the hulking thing of wood, bronze and stone will soak up wounds and even spells meant for the wearer. This one's master died long ago. With no one left to protect, it guards the room and treats every visitor as the assassin.

homunculus.name: Homunculus
homunculus.lore: The alchemist Paracelsus is credited with a recipe for the homunculus, a tiny artificial man grown in a sealed flask. Wizards improved on the idea: a bat-winged servant a foot tall, made with a pint of the maker's own blood. It sees for its master, carries messages, and cannot speak. Its bite brings on sleep, which suits a master who wants subjects delivered alive.

clockwork_horror.name: Clockwork Horror
clockwork_horror.lore: A brass spider the size of a mastiff, ticking. Its legs end in spinning saws, and a spark jumps between the copper prongs where a head should be. Clockwork horrors mend one another from the scrap of their own fallen, so a nest never shrinks. The artificers who built them as assassins are long dead. Nobody remains who knows the word that stops them.

displacer_beast.name: Displacer Beast
displacer_beast.lore: A six-legged panther-like predator that projects a displaced image of itself, appearing to be slightly to the side of its actual location. This ability makes it infuriatingly difficult to strike while its two tentacles are lethally accurate. Displacer beasts hate blink dogs with an ancient and implacable passion.

owlbear.name: Owlbear
owlbear.lore: A miserable alchemical accident or experiment fused the savagery of a bear with the precision and ferocity of a great owl. The owlbear is perpetually hungry, furious, and difficult to reason with. Despite the chaos of its origin it breeds true, suggesting it is now a permanent fixture of the dungeon ecosystem.

black_pudding.name: Black Pudding
black_pudding.lore: A heap of living tar that creeps along floor, wall and ceiling alike. It eats wood, leather and steel, and a sword that goes in comes out as a pitted stump. Worse, a blade does not wound it: each cut piece crawls off as a smaller pudding. Lightning does the same. Old hands burn it, and stand well back while they do.

gray_ooze.name: Gray Ooze
gray_ooze.lore: It looks like a patch of wet stone, and it lies as still as one until a boot comes down in it. Then the patch rears up and strikes like a snake. Its slime eats metal with frightening speed, and mail rusts through in the time it takes to say a prayer. Fire and frost, the usual answers to slimes, do nothing to it.

ochre_jelly.name: Ochre Jelly
ochre_jelly.lore: A mustard-yellow blob that can squeeze under a door or through a crack no wider than a finger, then pour itself down a corridor faster than a man can jog. It cannot eat metal or stone, only flesh and leather, and it is thorough about both. A sword stroke or a lightning bolt merely divides it into two hungry jellies.

piercer.name: Piercer
piercer.lore: A piercer is a cave snail that has taken its trade to an extreme. Its shell is a stone spike as long as a man's arm, and it hangs point down among the real stalactites, listening. When footsteps pass underneath, it lets go. A hit is usually final. A miss leaves it helpless on the floor, inching back toward the wall for the long climb up.

lurker_above.name: Lurker Above
lurker_above.lore: A broad, flat creature like a manta ray, with a hide that copies the colour and grain of the ceiling it clings to. It can hang there for months without feeding. When something warm walks beneath, it lets go, lands like a wet blanket, and wraps tight. The careful delver who checked every floor tile seldom thinks to look up.

trapper.name: Trapper
trapper.lore: The floor-dwelling cousin of the lurker above. A trapper spreads itself thin across a chamber and matches the flagstones so exactly that it sometimes raises a lump in its middle shaped like a chest, as bait. It waits for weight at its centre, then folds shut like a closing fist. Veteran delvers prod the floor ahead with a long pole for exactly this reason.

roper.name: Roper
roper.lore: A stalagmite-like ambush predator with six sticky strands it can extend up to fifty feet. When a strand attaches it drains vitality from the victim while drawing them inexorably toward the roper's enormous toothy maw. They are disturbingly intelligent and seem to take pleasure in their prey's struggles.

carrion_crawler.name: Carrion Crawler
carrion_crawler.lore: A pale green caterpillar as long as a horse, with a ring of eight wet tentacles around its mouth. It eats the dead and keeps the dungeon corridors clean of them, which would be a service if it did not also like its food fresh. One touch of a tentacle stiffens a limb. Its slime trail on the stone marks a hunting ground.

rot_grub_swarm.name: Rot Grub Swarm
rot_grub_swarm.lore: Fat white maggots the length of a finger, hundreds of them, boiling in a midden heap or a dead thing's ribs. They sense warmth and chew toward it. A grub that reaches skin burrows in at once and heads for the heart. The accepted remedy is a hot brand on the spot, applied immediately, and nobody who has needed it complains about the scar.

otyugh.name: Otyugh
otyugh.lore: Three stumpy legs, a barrel body that is mostly mouth, two long tentacles lined with thorny ridges, and a third stalk that carries its eyes above the muck. The otyugh lives in the dungeon's rubbish pit and eats what falls in. Some dungeon keepers feed one on purpose. Its bite carries every filth it has ever swallowed, and the wound goes bad quickly.

xorn.name: Xorn
xorn.lore: A three-armed, three-legged alien from the Elemental Plane of Earth. The xorn can phase through solid rock and has an exceptional sense for metals and gems, which it consumes for sustenance. It will negotiate for gold or gems and only fights when cornered or denied its prize.

gnoll_pack_lord.name: Gnoll Pack Lord
gnoll_pack_lord.lore: The medieval bestiary says the hyena digs up graves and imitates human voices to call men out of their houses at night. Gnolls are that animal on two legs, and the pack lord is the biggest of them, scarred from every challenge it has won. The pack fights harder under its eye. Kill it, and the rest fall to quarrelling over the succession.

lizardfolk.name: Lizardfolk
lizardfolk.lore: Scaled marsh dwellers, tall as men, who have lived in the same wet caves since before the dungeon had walls. A lizardfolk hunter feels no hatred for an intruder and no pity either. It sees meat, tools, and a threat to the nest, in that order. They waste nothing they kill. Cold makes them sluggish, and they avoid the icy levels.

lizardfolk_shaman.name: Lizardfolk Shaman
lizardfolk_shaman.lore: The eldest of the warren, hung with snake skulls and turtle shell, who speaks for the spirits of marsh and egg. The shaman brews venom from swamp adders and can spit it farther than a man throws a knife. The tribe does nothing without a reading of the signs. When the shaman falls, the hunters stop and wait for an omen that will not come.

troglodyte.name: Troglodyte
troglodyte.lore: The Greeks used 'troglodyte', cave-goer, for the cave-dwelling tribes they heard of along the Red Sea. The dungeon's troglodytes earn the word more grimly: squat grey lizard-men who have never seen the sun. Frightened or angry, a troglodyte sweats an oil so rank that grown warriors double over. They raid for meat and steel, and the tribe eats its own weak.

kobold_sorcerer.name: Kobold Sorcerer
kobold_sorcerer.lore: In German mining lore the kobold was a spiteful sprite of the deep shafts, and miners named the troublesome ore cobalt after it. The small scaled kobolds of the dungeon claim dragons as their ancestors. Now and then one is born who can prove it, with fire at its fingertips. The tribe treats that one as royalty and still expects it to run first.

bullywug.name: Bullywug
bullywug.lore: Frog-men of the flooded levels, slick, pop-eyed and loud. A bullywug can clear a moat at a bound and usually lands spear first. Each petty chief calls himself a king and demands tribute from the next pool over, so they are always at war with one another. Stronger monsters hire them cheaply, paying in territory nobody else wants.

kuo_toa.name: Kuo-Toa
kuo_toa.lore: Fish-headed folk of the sunless seas, with bulging eyes that never close and skin that glistens with slime. Long ages in the dark broke something in them. They build gods out of driftwood, bones and rumor, then worship the result so fiercely that their priests work real wonders in its name. Their shields are smeared with a glue that grips any blade that strikes them.

behir_lesser.name: Lesser Behir
behir_lesser.lore: Forty feet of blue-scaled serpent carried on a dozen clawed legs, able to run up a cliff face as easily as along a floor. Lightning gathers behind its teeth and comes out in a single straight stroke. What survives that, it wraps and squeezes. Behirs hate dragons beyond reason and will abandon a kill to go and fight one.

catoblepas.name: Catoblepas
catoblepas.lore: Pliny the Elder placed the catoblepas near the source of the Nile: a sluggish beast whose head is so heavy that it always hangs toward the ground. The name is Greek for 'the one that looks downward'. Pliny counted this a mercy to mankind, because anyone who meets its eyes drops dead. Down here it grazes on poisonous weeds and, now and then, looks up.

cockatrice.name: Cockatrice
cockatrice.lore: Medieval bestiaries say the cockatrice hatches from an egg laid by an old rooster and brooded by a toad. It has a cock's head and wings on a serpent's body, and its touch stiffens flesh toward stone. The same books name its two terrors: the weasel, which alone can fight it unharmed, and the crow of a rooster, which kills it.

darkmantle.name: Darkmantle
darkmantle.lore: It hangs from the cave roof with its tentacles drawn up, looking like one more stalactite. When a lantern passes beneath, the darkmantle spills a blackness no flame can push back, then drops and wraps its webbed body around the nearest head. The victim is blind, smothered, and wearing the enemy as a hood. Friends hesitate to swing.

ettercap.name: Ettercap
ettercap.lore: 'Ettercap' is an old Scots word for a spider, from the Old English 'attercoppe', poison-head. The dungeon's ettercap is a hunched grey creature with a spider's fangs and spinnerets and a shepherd's habits. It keeps giant spiders as a herd, strings snares across every corridor of its range, and waits while trapped prey wears itself out before it comes to bite.

grick.name: Grick
grick.lore: A rubbery worm as thick as a man's thigh, the colour of the rock it hides in, with four barbed tentacles around a snapping beak. It wedges itself into a crack and strikes at whatever passes. Its hide gives like wet leather under an ordinary blade and takes little hurt. Once fed, it sleeps for days in its hole. Unfed, it will follow a party for miles.

hook_horror.name: Hook Horror
hook_horror.lore: It stands nine feet tall on a beetle's armored body, with a vulture's beak and, in place of hands, a pair of bony hooks as long as scythes. Hook horrors talk by clacking those hooks against the cave wall, and the sound carries a long way. Delvers who hear clicking in the dark count the different rhythms. That is the size of the pack.

phase_spider.name: Phase Spider
phase_spider.lore: A spider as large as a pony, pale blue and banded, that hunts from the misty border realm lying alongside the solid world. It steps through, bites, and steps back before a sword can answer. Victims describe an empty corridor and a sudden pain. Assassins pay well for its venom, though collecting it has cost more lives than the venom has taken.

wyvern.name: Wyvern
wyvern.lore: English heralds drew a careful line: a dragon has four legs, a wyvern only two, with wings for forelimbs and a barbed, knotted tail. The living animal lacks a dragon's mind and breath, and makes up the difference with temper. It swoops, pins its prey with its talons, and drives the tail sting in from above. The poison works fast.

skeleton_archer.name: Skeleton Archer
skeleton_archer.lore: Bowmen who fell at their posts and were ordered back up. No sinew is left to draw the string, yet the bow bends and the shaft flies as true as it did in life. Arrows sent in answer rattle through the ribs and out the other side. A mace does better. The quiver never runs dry, and nobody has seen one being filled.

skeleton_warrior.name: Skeleton Warrior
skeleton_warrior.lore: Men-at-arms of some buried kingdom, still in their rusted mail, still holding the shield wall their captain taught them. The drill outlasted the flesh. They advance in step, cover one another, and bash with the shield rim when the sword is turned. The spell that raised them is older than any living warlock can read.

skeleton_mage.name: Skeleton Mage
skeleton_mage.lore: A wizard who would not put his books down, even for death. The robes hang on bare ribs, and a pale light crawls between the finger bones when it lifts a hand. It still knows its spells, though it has forgotten why it learned them. Necromancers prize the skull, which keeps a whisper of everything it once memorized.

burning_skeleton.name: Burning Skeleton
burning_skeleton.lore: A skeleton wrapped in flame that neither consumes the bones nor ever goes out. Dungeon tradition holds that these were men who bargained with fire demons and were paid in full. The blaze is its weapon and its shield, and everything it touches catches. Cold water hisses on it, and the hot bones crack.

frost_skeleton.name: Frost Skeleton
frost_skeleton.lore: Soldiers who froze on a winter march and never thawed. Rime covers the bones in a blue-white crust, icicles hang from the jaw, and a low mist follows at ankle height wherever one walks. Its touch fastens ice onto flesh. A torch undoes it quickly, since the frost is all that holds the joints together.

zombie_hulk.name: Zombie Hulk
zombie_hulk.lore: A necromancer's battering ram. The maker takes the largest corpse to hand and pumps it with dark power until the muscles swell and split the skin. It is slow, and it never needs to be quick. It plods to a door, a wall or a shield line and beats it flat with fists the size of anvils.

plague_zombie.name: Plague Zombie
plague_zombie.lore: During the Black Death the gravediggers could not keep pace, and the dead went into pits by the hundred. What climbs out of such a pit carries the sickness still. Its fingers are black, its breath is foul, and a scratch or a bite passes on the fever that killed it. Fire is the old remedy for plague houses, and it serves here too.

rotting_zombie.name: Rotting Zombie
rotting_zombie.lore: A corpse raised with the cheapest spell a necromancer knows. It has no skill and no thought. Sinew and bad magic hold it together, and pieces drop off as it walks. It comes forward at a shuffle, arms out, and stops for no wound short of ruin. One is a nuisance. A corridor full of them is a wall that bites.

ghast.name: Ghast
ghast.lore: The ghoul's cleverer cousin. A ghast keeps enough of its mind to lay an ambush, post a lookout, and lead the pack that feeds beside it. Its claws lock the muscles of whatever they scratch, and the reek of an opened grave rolls ahead of it so thickly that soldiers retch before they can raise a shield. It keeps tokens from its most memorable hunts.

gravehound.name: Gravehound
gravehound.lore: Kings were buried with their hunting dogs so the pack could run beside them in the next world. Tomb robbers woke these ones instead. They are bone and dried hide now, and they hunt exactly as they did alive: one drives, two flank, and the jaws that close on a hamstring do not open again.

poltergeist.name: Poltergeist
poltergeist.lore: The word is German for 'noisy ghost'. A poltergeist has no shape to show, only a temper: doors slam, crockery flies, a chair skates across the room and breaks against the wall. It is the spirit of someone who died bewildered and has stayed that way. It does not hunt the living. It rages at them for being able to leave.

revenant.name: Revenant
revenant.lore: The chronicler William of Newburgh recorded several revenants in twelfth-century England: wicked men who climbed out of their graves at night to plague their towns, until the neighbours dug up the bodies and burned them. A revenant returns for one reason, a wrong it means to repay. It will walk through sword cuts to reach the throat it remembers.

allip.name: Allip
allip.lore: The remnant of a mind that broke before the body died. An allip is a twist of darkness shaped vaguely like a person, and it mutters without pause: half a prayer, a child's rhyme, a list of names. Listeners catch themselves following the thread, and that is how it gets in. Its touch brings a heavy, dreamless stupor.

haunting_presence.name: Haunting Presence
haunting_presence.lore: Something terrible happened in this room, and a little of the person it happened to never left. The presence has no face and no voice. It is a cold spot, a held breath, the certainty of being watched from the corner. Then the dread arrives all at once, and strong men find themselves running before they have decided to.

fetch.name: Fetch
fetch.lore: In Irish folklore a fetch is the exact double of a living person. Seen in the morning, it promises long life. Seen at dusk, it means that person's death is near. The dungeon's fetches have turned the omen into a trade. One wears the face of whoever looks at it, walks toward them smiling, and drinks their life at a touch.

shade.name: Shade
shade.lore: When Odysseus sailed to the edge of the world to question the dead, the shades crowded round his trench of sheep's blood, voiceless and thin until they had drunk. Homer's ghosts are like that: memories without strength, hungry for warmth. The shades below never got their sip. They gather wherever the light is poor, and dim it further.

will_o_wisp.name: Will-o-Wisp
will_o_wisp.lore: Marsh travelers across Europe knew the pale light that bobs ahead on the path like a lantern and leads straight into the bog. Scholars named it ignis fatuus, 'foolish fire'. Country people called it Will with the wisp, or Jack with the lantern. In the dungeon the light is a spiteful ghost that feeds on the terror of the lost. Its touch jolts like lightning.

soul_shadow.name: Soul Shadow
soul_shadow.lore: Where many die together in terror, in a massacre or a collapsed mine, the souls sometimes tangle and cannot part. The knot becomes one thing: a mass of darkness in which faces surface and sink. None of them agrees with the others except in pain. It folds over the living and pulls, and whatever it tears free joins the crowd inside.

death_echo.name: Death Echo
death_echo.lore: No ghost stands behind a death echo. The place itself remembers. A murder or a last stand struck so hard that the moment was stamped into the stone, and it plays again and again: the same scream, the same fall. Whoever walks into the scene is given a part in it, and the echo strikes at them as it struck then.

vampire_thrall.name: Vampire Thrall
vampire_thrall.lore: In Bram Stoker's novel, the madman Renfield serves Count Dracula from an asylum cell, eating flies and begging for his master's notice. Every vampire keeps such servants: mortals fed a few drops of the master's blood, stronger than they should be and incapable of disloyalty. A thrall still has a pulse of sorts. It would spend it gladly to buy its master one more night.

nosferatu.name: Nosferatu
nosferatu.lore: Emily Gerard, a Scottish writer living in Transylvania, set the word down in 1885 as the local name for a vampire, and Bram Stoker carried it into Dracula. Nothing courtly survives in this breed. It is bald, rat-toothed and long-fingered, a thing of plague cellars that hunts alone. It hates the dawn above all, and the dungeon has no dawn.

strigoi.name: Strigoi
strigoi.lore: Romanian villagers named it from the Latin strix, the screech owl that drank blood by night. A strigoi is a troubled dead man who climbs out of his grave and goes home first, feeding on his own family before the neighbours. The old remedies were garlic in the mouth, a stake through the heart, and fire. Its claws carry grave sickness.

jiangshi.name: Jiangshi
jiangshi.lore: The Chinese hopping corpse. Death stiffened its limbs, so it bounds forward with both arms held straight out, still dressed in the robes of a Qing official. It finds the living by their breath, and a traveller who holds his breath may pass unseen. A paper talisman pressed to its forehead stops it cold.
