Peach wood, mirrors and a rooster's crow all drive it back.

vrykolakas.name: Vrykolakas
vrykolakas.lore: The restless dead of the Greek islands. Its corpse does not rot. It swells tight as a drum and walks the village by night, knocking on doors and calling a name once. Whoever answers dies within days, so islanders learned never to answer a first knock. Around 1700 the French botanist Tournefort watched the people of Mykonos burn one.

demi_lich.name: Demi-Lich
demi_lich.lore: A lich so ancient that its body has crumbled away, leaving only the skull which houses its immortal consciousness. The demi-lich has transcended physical existence almost entirely, its soul focused into the gems embedded in its eye sockets. Its very wail can trap the souls of the living, and it commands magic beyond mortal comprehension.

lich_thrall.name: Lich Thrall
lich_thrall.lore: Lich is the Old English word for a corpse, and the lych-gate of a churchyard is where the coffin once rested before burial. A lich's thrall is a lesser sorcerer raised to serve the greater one: steward, doorkeeper, and spare pair of hands. It remembers its spells and its oath, and nothing else. Its cold fingers lock the joints of anyone it touches.

death_mage.name: Death Mage
death_mage.lore: Scripture tells how King Saul, who had outlawed the art himself, went in disguise by night to the witch of Endor and bade her call up the dead prophet Samuel. Samuel came, and told Saul he would die the next day. The death mage has made that forbidden trade a life's study, and has gone halfway into the grave to learn it better.

bone_witch.name: Bone Witch
bone_witch.lore: Russian tales know her kind as Baba Yaga the Bony-Legged, whose hut stands on chicken legs behind a fence of human bones with a skull on every post. This one has gone further and kept nothing but the bones. She hangs her lair with what her enemies leave behind, and she throws the sharper pieces. Spear points slip between her ribs. A hammer does not.

necromancer_lord.name: Necromancer Lord
necromancer_lord.lore: Koschei the Deathless, the sorcerer of Russian tales, could not be killed because his death was not in his body. He hid it in a needle, in an egg, in a duck, in a hare, in an iron chest under an oak on the island of Buyan. A necromancer lord has learned the same trick. His servants are the dead, and one of them carries what he fears to lose.

pale_master.name: Pale Master
pale_master.lore: A necromancer who would not wait for death. The pale master replaces his own failing parts with grave goods: a dead man's hand stitched at the wrist, borrowed ribs, eyes that no longer blink. Each graft makes him colder and harder to tell from his servants. He knows exactly how a body comes apart, and his touch stops a limb as surely as a surgeon's knife.

wight_lord.name: Wight Lord
wight_lord.lore: The Icelandic Eyrbyggja Saga tells of Thorolf Lame-Foot, a bitter old man who would not stay in his grave. He walked the valley killing shepherds and cattle, and the men he killed were seen walking in his company. Only burning his body to ash ended it. A wight lord rules the same way: every victim it drains joins its household.

barrow_wight.name: Barrow Wight
barrow_wight.lore: In Grettir's Saga the outlaw Grettir broke into the mound of Kar the Old and found the dead man seated on his throne among his treasure. Kar seized him, and they wrestled through the dark until Grettir cut off his head. A barrow wight is that kind of dead: a chieftain who will not give up his gold, with a grip that stops the breath.

cairn_wight.name: Cairn Wight
cairn_wight.lore: A cairn is a heap of stones raised over the dead, and in the Scottish Highlands every passer-by added one. To promise a stone on a man's cairn was to promise to remember him. The dead beneath a neglected cairn remember being forgotten. This wight had no hall and no gold, only a pile of rocks on a hillside, and it resents the living all the more for it.

crypt_thing.name: Crypt Thing
crypt_thing.lore: A unique form of undead guardian created specifically to protect tombs without causing harm to the protected dead within. Rather than attacking intruders directly, crypt things teleport trespassers to random locations in the dungeon, separating adventuring parties and leaving individuals lost and alone. They cannot be reasoned with or bribed.

grave_guardian.name: Grave Guardian
grave_guardian.lore: Champions who swore before they died to keep watch over holy ground, and were buried standing at the door of the crypt with sword in hand. The oath holds them, not a necromancer. They still carry a spark of the blessing laid on them, which makes other dead things shy away, and they strike down anyone who comes to dig, robber and crusader alike.

tomb_guardian.name: Tomb Guardian
tomb_guardian.lore: The first emperor of China, Qin Shi Huang, went into his tomb guarded by some eight thousand soldiers of fired clay, each with a different face. Lesser kings could not afford clay and used men. A tomb guardian is a picked soldier sealed in with his lord and bound to one doorway forever. The nearer a thief comes to the burial chamber, the harder it fights.

ossuary_horror.name: Ossuary Horror
ossuary_horror.lore: At Sedlec in Bohemia the bones of tens of thousands of dead were stacked into pyramids and strung into a chandelier said to hold every bone in the human body. Bones kept in such numbers forget whose they were. An ossuary horror is a charnel house that has stood up: a rolling drift of skulls and long bones that adds each kill to the pile.

mohrg.name: Mohrg
mohrg.lore: The corpse of a murderer who died unrepentant and unpunished, still doing in death what it did in life. Its ribs hang open and a long purple tongue coils where the heart should be. One touch of that tongue locks every muscle in the body. Those it kills rise within days and follow it, so a mohrg seldom walks alone for long.

huecuva.name: Huecuva
huecuva.lore: The Mapuche of Chile gave the name huecuvu to spirits that brought blight and sickness. Down here it belongs to a priest who broke his vows and died unforgiven. It still wears the rags of its vestments and can put on the look of a living cleric to draw the trusting close. Its scratch festers. Honest prayer is the one thing it still fears.

lesser_death.name: Lesser Death
lesser_death.lore: The Greeks called Death by name: Thanatos, brother of Sleep. Sisyphus once tricked him into his own chains, and for a time no one on earth could die. Heracles wrestled him at a graveside and won back Queen Alcestis. A lesser death is a small shadow of that power, a reaper sent for one soul at a time. It can be beaten, as the stories show.

greater_shadow.name: Greater Shadow
greater_shadow.lore: When Odysseus sailed to the edge of the world to question the dead, he dug a trench and filled it with sheep's blood. The shades came crowding to drink, because only blood could give them back their voices. A greater shadow has drunk for centuries. It fills a room like spilled ink and takes the strength out of every arm inside it.

nightshade_spawn.name: Nightshade Spawn
nightshade_spawn.lore: Offspring of true nightshade creatures, these lesser versions of the nightshade family are still among the most powerful undead a dungeon delver is likely to encounter. They embody the concept of negative energy given physical form, corrupting and desecrating everything around them. Plants wither, fire dims, and hope fades in their presence.

forsaken_shell.name: Forsaken Shell
forsaken_shell.lore: An animated body from which the soul has been violently ripped, leaving a hollow vessel that moves on pure necromantic energy alone. The forsaken shell retains no memories or personality of its former occupant. They are sometimes created deliberately by necromancers who need the soul for other purposes but want to keep the body useful.

hollow_one.name: Hollow One
hollow_one.lore: A person who traded away their soul through dark bargains, died, and now walks as an undead creature of perpetual hunger. The hollow one seeks souls to fill the void where their own used to be, but no soul can permanently fill the absence. They are pitiable creatures, driven mad by an emptiness that cannot be sated.

charnel_hound.name: Charnel Hound
charnel_hound.lore: Old English and Scandinavian custom held that the first one buried in a new churchyard had to stay and guard it, so builders buried a dog there first to spare a human soul the duty. That guardian was called the church grim. A charnel hound is the necromancer's copy: a pack's worth of dog bones wired into one tireless tracker that never loses a scent.

dread_knight.name: Dread Knight
dread_knight.lore: Fallen paladins who have become undead warriors of darkness, their divine power twisted into unholy strength. They retain their martial prowess and tactical intelligence from life, making them among the most dangerous undead combatants. Their armor seems to absorb light, and their gaze carries the weight of condemned souls.

bone_archer.name: Bone Archer
bone_archer.lore: A dead bowman set on a ledge and told to shoot at anything warm. It whittles its shafts from its own spare ribs and never runs short, since the dungeon keeps it supplied with more. An arrow shot back at it mostly passes through the gaps. It will not close to fight, and it has all the patience of a thing with nowhere else to be.

skeletal_giant.name: Skeletal Giant
skeletal_giant.lore: Herodotus tells how the Spartans dug up a coffin seven cubits long at Tegea and carried the huge bones home as those of the hero Orestes. The ancient world was full of such finds, and people drew the natural conclusion: giants once walked here. Some of those bones have been made to walk again. Each fist is the size of a millstone, and it comes down like one.

undead_dragon_lesser.name: Lesser Undead Dragon
undead_dragon_lesser.lore: Cadmus killed the dragon of Ares at the spring of Thebes and sowed its teeth in the ground, and armed men sprang up from the furrows. A dragon's bones do not lie quiet. This one was raised whole by a necromancer with more ambition than sense. The fire in its chest has gone out, and what it breathes now is the cold of the grave.

lich_dragon_spawn.name: Lich Dragon Spawn
lich_dragon_spawn.lore: A dragon lives for a thousand years and still fears the end. The oldest and proudest let a lich bind their souls into a hoarded gem, and rise again as bone and cold sorcery. This is the get of such a creature, hatched dead from a clutch laid before the rite. It never drew a living breath. It has a dragon's cunning and none of a dragon's warmth, and its bite stops the heart.

ethereal_filcher.name: Ethereal Filcher
ethereal_filcher.lore: An incorporeal undead that phases between the material and ethereal planes to steal objects from the living. Ethereal filchers are drawn to bright or magical items, which they collect in hidden ethereal lairs. They are rarely aggressive unless cornered, preferring to flee with their stolen goods rather than risk destruction.

nightmare_shade.name: Nightmare Shade
nightmare_shade.lore: Ovid names three sons of Sleep who shape the dreams of men. Morpheus plays the human parts. His brother Phobetor, the Frightener, takes the forms of beasts and monsters. A nightmare shade is a bad dream that outlived its dreamer, someone who died in terror. It looks into a mind, finds the worst thing there, and wears it.

soul_eater_spawn.name: Soul Eater Spawn
soul_eater_spawn.lore: The Egyptians feared a second death. In the Hall of Judgment the heart was weighed against the feather of Ma'at, and a heart heavy with wrongdoing was thrown to Ammit: crocodile head, lion forequarters, hippopotamus behind. A soul she ate was simply gone. Soul eater spawn are small, hungry things of her kind. They wait for no verdict before they feed.

dread_wraith.name: Dread Wraith
dread_wraith.lore: Ancient wraiths of tremendous power, dread wraiths are what common wraiths aspire to become after centuries of draining life from the living. They are rarely seen as they prefer to operate from the ethereal plane, reaching through to drain victims without exposing themselves to retaliation. The area around a dread wraith is perpetually cold and lightless.

nightwing.name: Nightwing
nightwing.lore: The greatest of the nightshade creatures, a nightwing appears as a vast bat-like shadow of impossible size that blots out stars as it passes overhead. They are engines of pure negative energy that desecrate the land they fly over, killing plant life and corrupting water sources. Ancient texts warn that a nightwing's arrival heralds a period of mass death and catastrophe.

crystal_ooze.name: crystal ooze
crystal_ooze.lore: A clear, slow jelly that grows a rind of mineral crystal wherever it rests, like rock candy on a string. In a gem seam it is nearly invisible until the wall begins to move. Whatever it touches it coats in a fast-setting crust that stiffens the joints. Miners test a suspect vein with a hammer: crystal rings, and the ooze cracks.

green_slime.name: green slime
green_slime.lore: It hangs from damp ceilings like wet moss and waits for something warm to walk underneath. Then it lets go. Green slime eats cloth, leather, wood and flesh, and turns all of it into more green slime. Scraping it off only spreads it. Old delvers carry a torch for the purpose, because fire and hard frost are the two things that kill it.

yellow_mold.name: yellow mold
yellow_mold.lore: A dry, sulphur-coloured crust on old wood and older bones. A footstep is enough to burst it, and the cloud of spores it throws up fills the lungs and then the head. Men who breathe it see doors that are not there and friends who are. The mold burns with a bright orange flame, which is the only safe way to clear a room of it.

brown_mold.name: brown mold
brown_mold.lore: Brown mold feeds on warmth the way other molds feed on damp. The air around a patch is bitter cold, and a hand held near it goes numb. Torches are worse than useless: fire feeds it, and a burning brand thrown at it can double the patch in a breath. Frost is what kills it. A cold snap turns it grey and dead in moments.

gibbering_slime.name: gibbering slime
gibbering_slime.lore: A heap of pale jelly covered in mouths, none of them finished, all of them talking. The mouths repeat scraps of every voice the slime has ever swallowed: prayers, bargains, a child's counting rhyme, somebody calling for a lamp. Stand near it long and the words begin to sound like sense. That is the moment it reaches out.

toxic_jelly.name: toxic jelly
toxic_jelly.lore: Bright green, wobbling, and poisonous clear through. The toxic jelly has no fangs and needs none: it simply folds over whatever blunders into it and lets the poison soak in. Rats that drink from a pool it has crossed die before they reach their holes. A dungeon corridor with no rats in it at all is worth a second look.

giant_scorpion.name: giant scorpion
giant_scorpion.lore: Orion the hunter boasted that he would kill every beast on earth, so the Earth sent a scorpion to sting him. Both were set among the stars, on opposite sides of the sky, and Orion still sets as the Scorpion rises. This one is the size of a pony. Its claws only hold the prey still. The work is done by the tail.

giant_wasp.name: giant wasp
giant_wasp.lore: A hunting wasp does not kill what it catches. It stings the prey to stillness, drags it to the nest, and lays an egg on it, so the grub hatches onto fresh meat. The nest is grey paper, chewed from wood: watching wasps gave the naturalist Reaumur the idea that paper could be made from trees. These are the size of hounds.

giant_beetle.name: giant beetle
giant_beetle.lore: A beetle's wing cases are its front wings, hardened into a shield that closes over the back like a clasped book. On a beetle the size of a boar that shield turns a sword edge well enough. The jaws work like a smith's tongs. It is not clever and not quick. A heavy blow that cracks the shell ends the matter.

giant_mantis.name: giant mantis
giant_mantis.lore: The Greeks named it mantis, the prophet, because it holds its forelegs folded like hands at prayer. It can turn its head to look straight behind it, which no beetle or wasp can do. The strike is over faster than an eye can blink, and the spined forelegs close like a trap. Grown to the height of a man, it waits just as patiently.

spider_queen.name: spider queen
spider_queen.lore: Arachne of Lydia wove so well that she challenged Athena herself, and her tapestry showed the gods at their worst without one flaw in the work. Athena tore it apart and turned the girl into a spider, to hang and weave forever. The spider queen is a monstrous daughter of that line. Her brood hunts where she sends it, and her hall is hung with silk and what the silk holds.

phase_spider_lesser.name: Lesser Phase Spider
phase_spider_lesser.lore: A spider that hunts from the wrong side of the air. It steps out of the world, walks to where its prey is standing, and steps back in with its fangs already closing. Then it is gone again before a sword can answer. The young ones manage only a short hop and must rest between. Its web shimmers faintly and holds things that are not quite there.

web_spinner.name: web spinner
web_spinner.lore: Spider silk is stronger than a steel wire of the same thickness and stretches like a bowstring before it breaks. The web spinner makes it by the yard. It strings a corridor from wall to wall, then sits back in a crack and lets the web do the fighting. It bites only what is already tangled. A torch clears its work in seconds.

death_beetle.name: death beetle
death_beetle.lore: The Egyptians laid a stone scarab over the heart of the dead, carved with a spell asking the heart not to speak against its owner at the judgment. In English sickrooms the tick of the deathwatch beetle in the timbers was counted an omen that the watch would soon end. This black-shelled giant is both in one: a tomb beetle whose rattle makes the limbs heavy.

giant_lizard.name: giant lizard
giant_lizard.lore: Many lizards have a third eye, a pale scale on the crown of the head that cannot see shapes but can tell light from dark and warns of a shadow passing overhead. This one is as long as a rowing boat and lies on warm stone near the dungeon's vents. Cold makes it sluggish. Warmed through, it is quicker than anything that size should be.

basilisk_lesser.name: lesser basilisk
basilisk_lesser.lore: Pliny describes the basilisk as a serpent of Cyrene no longer than twelve fingers, with a white mark on its head like a crown. Its breath withers bushes and splits stone. Later writers added that it hatches from a cock's egg brooded by a toad, and that a weasel, a mirror, or a rooster's crow will kill it. A young one's stare only locks the limbs.

rock_python.name: rock python
rock_python.lore: The rock python is the largest snake in Africa and can swallow an antelope whole, horns and all. It does not crush its prey. Each time the animal breathes out the coils draw tighter, until the heart can no longer push blood. Then the jaws walk forward over the meal, one side at a time. In the dungeon it lies among fallen stone and looks like more of it.

komodo_brute.name: komodo brute
komodo_brute.lore: For a long time people believed the Komodo dragon killed with a filthy mouth and waited for wounds to fester. The truth is worse: it has venom glands in its lower jaw, and the venom keeps blood from clotting. Its saw-edged teeth open the wound, the prey weakens and wanders off, and the dragon follows the scent at its leisure. This breed is bigger.

giant_frog.name: giant frog
giant_frog.lore: A frog's tongue is fixed at the front of its mouth, not the back, and flips out and home again faster than a blink. To swallow, the frog pulls its eyes down into its skull and uses them to push the meal along. A frog the size of a calf does all this to things the size of a helmet. It sits in black water with only its eyes showing.

mud_crawler.name: mud crawler
mud_crawler.lore: A squat, plated reptile of underground rivers, somewhere between a snapping turtle and a crocodile. It lies in the silt until the mud dries on its back in a second shell, and a sword edge skids off the crust. It is slow on land. Its hooked claws are not, and once they are set it holds on and lets its weight do the rest.

swamp_serpent.name: swamp serpent
swamp_serpent.lore: A thick-bodied water snake of flooded passages. Like the cottonmouth of the southern swamps, it warns before it strikes: it coils, throws back its head and gapes to show the white lining of its mouth. That is the only courtesy it offers. Its venom breaks down blood and flesh around the bite. It swims with its whole body on the surface, head held high.

sea_snake.name: sea snake
sea_snake.lore: Sea snakes are cousins of the cobra that went back to the water. The tail has flattened into a paddle, one lung runs nearly the length of the body, and some can draw air through their skin and stay under for hours. Drop for drop, the venom is among the strongest of any serpent's, and it stills the muscles. The flooded lower halls suit it well.

dire_lion.name: dire lion
dire_lion.lore: Lions once hunted across Europe. The painters of Chauvet cave drew them on the rock by torchlight some thirty thousand years ago: a whole pride in profile, stalking bison, the males without manes. Those cave lions stood taller than any lion alive now. The dungeon has kept a few. They hunt in the dark as their kind always did.

dire_bear.name: dire bear
dire_bear.lore: Cave bears wintered so deep underground, and for so many thousands of years, that their fur polished the rock walls smooth where they squeezed past. Their claw marks are still there, higher than a man can reach. This is that bear, or something very like it. It does not go looking for trouble. Anything that walks into its sleeping chamber is trouble enough.

wolf_pack_leader.name: wolf pack leader
wolf_pack_leader.lore: A wolf pack is a family: a mated pair and their grown young. The leader is not the fiercest fighter but the parent, the one who chooses the trail and begins the hunt. Its howl carries for miles and tells every wolf in hearing where to be. Men who hear it close by, in the dark, tend to forget what they were planning.

werewolf.name: werewolf
werewolf.lore: Ovid tells that King Lycaon of Arcadia doubted his guest was truly Zeus and tested him by serving human flesh at table. Zeus brought the house down in fire, and Lycaon fled howling into the fields with grey fur spreading over his arms, a wolf with the same savage eyes. Every werewolf carries that old sentence. Silver is the surest answer to it.

werewolf_alpha.name: werewolf alpha
werewolf_alpha.lore: In the Volsunga Saga, Sigmund and his son Sinfjotli found two wolf skins hanging in a forest hut, put them on, and could not take them off. They ran as wolves and spoke in howls, until Sigmund, in a rage, bit his own son in the throat. When the skins came loose at last they burned them. The alpha never burned its skin. It has worn the wolf for centuries and chooses to.

werebear.name: werebear
werebear.lore: Bodvar Bjarki, greatest champion of King Hrolf Kraki, fought the king's last battle as a huge bear that no weapon could bite, while his own body sat in a trance far behind the line. When a friend shook him awake, the bear vanished and the battle was lost. His father had been cursed into a bear's shape by day. The dungeon's werebears have the curse without the cause.

wererat.name: wererat
wererat.lore: Rats thrive wherever men store grain and throw out scraps, and the wererat has taken the lesson to heart. It lives in the drains under better creatures' halls, steals, listens, and sells what it hears. In a fight it prefers a knife in the back and a quick exit through a hole too small to follow. Its bite carries fever, and sometimes the curse itself.

weretiger.name: weretiger
weretiger.lore: Malay villagers told of the harimau jadian, a man who becomes a tiger after dark. The men of Kerinci in the highlands of Sumatra had the reputation of it, and travellers from that country were watched closely at night. Unlike the wolf-men of Europe, many were said to change at will. This one hunts as a tiger does: alone, from behind, after a long patient stalk.

winter_wolf.name: winter wolf
winter_wolf.lore: The Norse said two wolves run across the sky. Skoll chases the sun and Hati chases the moon, and at the end of the world each will catch its prey. Winter wolves are counted among their kin: white, horse-high, clever enough to speak, and cold to the bone. Frost giants keep them as hounds. Their breath freezes a man where he stands.

blink_dog.name: blink dog
blink_dog.lore: Blink dogs are intelligent teleporting canines that live in packs and are considered a good omen by travelers. They teleport short distances to attack and immediately blink away, making them extremely hard to pin down. Despite their chaotic fighting style they are deeply loyal creatures who can be befriended.

death_dog.name: death dog
death_dog.lore: Orthrus was the two-headed hound that guarded the red cattle of Geryon at the western edge of the world, and a brother to Cerberus. Heracles killed him with one blow of his club when he came for the herd. Death dogs are the same breed gone to seed. Both heads bite, and the wounds rot rather than heal. They keep company with the dead.

giant_eagle.name: giant eagle
giant_eagle.lore: A Mesopotamian tale older than Homer tells of Etana, king of Kish, who had no heir. He rescued a great eagle from a pit, and in thanks it carried him on its back toward heaven to seek the plant of birth, so high that land and sea shrank to nothing beneath them. Eagles of that size still nest above the dungeon's deepest shafts.

roc_chick.name: roc chick
roc_chick.lore: On Sinbad's fifth voyage his shipmates found a white dome on an island, broke it open with stones, and roasted the chick inside. It was a roc's egg. The parents came back, each carrying a boulder bigger than the ship, and sank it. A chick that does hatch soon stands taller than a horse and eats anything it can hold down.

roc_adult.name: Adult Roc
roc_adult.lore: Sinbad escaped a desert island by tying himself with his turban to the leg of a sleeping roc, which never noticed the weight. Marco Polo reported the bird from the seas near Madagascar: strong enough to lift an elephant, carry it high, and drop it to break on the rocks. Its wings span a hall. When it stoops, the wind arrives first.

stirge_swarm.name: stirge swarm
stirge_swarm.lore: The Romans feared the strix, a night bird that slipped into nurseries to drink the blood of infants, and Ovid tells how one was driven from the cradle of the infant prince Proca with a branch of whitethorn. The stirge borrows its name and habits: a bat-winged thing the size of a fist with a beak like an awl. One is a nuisance. They never come as one.

tengu_warrior.name: tengu warrior
tengu_warrior.lore: The crow-headed tengu of Japan's mountains are proud, quarrelsome, and the finest swordsmen alive. Legend says the boy Ushiwakamaru, later the great general Minamoto no Yoshitsune, slipped out of his temple on Mount Kurama each night to learn the sword from Sojobo, king of the tengu. They carry feather fans that raise a gale. They despise arrogance in everyone but themselves.

thunderbird_lesser.name: lesser thunderbird
thunderbird_lesser.lore: From the Great Lakes to the Pacific coast, the peoples of North America tell of the Thunderbird. Thunder is the beat of its wings and lightning flashes when it opens its eyes. It wars without end against the horned serpents and water panthers of the deep places. This smaller cousin has followed that war underground. Sparks crawl over its feathers, and its cry rattles teeth.

pixie_swarm.name: pixie swarm
pixie_swarm.lore: In Devon and Cornwall a traveller who wandered in circles all night on a moor he knew well was said to be pixy-led. The cure was to turn his coat inside out. One pixie is a finger-high prankster. A swarm is a cloud of them, armed with thorns and a dust that brings sleep on the spot. They dislike armour and anyone wearing it.

redcap.name: redcap
redcap.lore: A goblin of the ruined peel towers along the Scottish Border, where blood was shed for centuries. He is a short old man with long teeth, iron-shod boots and a pikestaff, and he keeps his cap red by soaking it in the blood of travellers. Human strength cannot stop him. Words of Scripture or the sight of a cross can: he shrieks and flees, leaving a tooth behind.

will_o_wisp_lesser.name: Lesser Will-o'-Wisp
will_o_wisp_lesser.lore: The Latin name is ignis fatuus, foolish fire. Country people called it Will of the Wisp, after a man named Will who carries a wisp of burning straw, or Jack of the Lantern. It is a pale flame that bobs over marsh at night, always a little farther off, until the follower is waist deep in the bog. Underground it favours pits. Blades pass through it.

green_hag.name: green hag
green_hag.lore: Lancashire children were warned away from ponds by the name of Jenny Greenteeth, who waits under the duckweed with long arms. On the River Tees she is Peg Powler, green-haired, and the froth on the water is her suds. A green hag is that kind of creature: a drowner who can look like a kindly old woman, or a young one, until her hands close.

sea_hag.name: sea hag
sea_hag.lore: Beowulf dived for most of a day through a haunted mere to reach the hall of Grendel's mother. The sword he carried would not bite her. He killed her with a giant-forged blade he found hanging on her own wall. Sea hags are of her sort: drowned-looking women of the cold deep, whose faces are hard to look at and harder to forget.

annis_hag.name: annis hag
annis_hag.lore: Black Annis of the Dane Hills near Leicester had a blue face and claws of iron. With those claws she dug her own cave out of the sandstone, and she crouched in the oak at its mouth to snatch lambs and children at dusk. Mothers said her teeth could be heard grinding from far off, in time to bar the door. Her kind are huge and brutally strong.

night_hag.name: night hag
night_hag.lore: The old Germanic peoples called her the mare. She comes at night, sits on a sleeper's chest, and presses out the breath, and the sleeper wakes unable to move or cry out. The word nightmare is her name. She rides the same victim night after night until nothing is left to ride. Country people kept iron by the bed against her.

satyr_trickster.name: satyr trickster
satyr_trickster.lore: Satyrs are the goat-legged followers of Dionysus: drinkers, dancers, and thieves of anything left unguarded. The god Pan, their wild cousin, chased the nymph Syrinx until she became a stand of reeds, and he cut the reeds into the first panpipes. A satyr with pipes can set a traveller's head spinning. He would rather rob than kill, and laughs either way.

dryad_guardian.name: dryad guardian
dryad_guardian.lore: A dryad's life is bound to her tree: drys is the Greek word for oak. When King Erysichthon cut down an oak in Demeter's sacred grove, the nymph inside cursed him with her last breath, and the goddess sent him a hunger that no feast could fill. Guardians remember that story. Roots rise where they point, and they do not wait for the axe.

leprechaun_hostile.name: hostile leprechaun
leprechaun_hostile.lore: The leprechaun is the fairy shoemaker of Ireland, found by the tap of his hammer. A man who holds him with his eyes can make him show his gold; one glance away and he is gone. One farmer tied a red garter to the bush that marked the spot and went for a spade. He came back to find a garter on every bush in the field. This one is tired of being grabbed.

spriggan.name: spriggan
spriggan.lore: Cornish folk said the spriggans were the ghosts of the old giants. They guard the treasure buried in cairns and hill forts, and though they look like small, ugly old men, they can swell to a giant's size when a digger's spade strikes stone. They also raise storms over standing crops and steal what is left unwatched. The gold they guard is seldom theirs.

boggart.name: boggart
boggart.lore: A Yorkshire farmer, worn out by the boggart that soured his milk and pinched his children, loaded the cart to move away. A neighbour asked if he was leaving. A voice from inside the butter churn answered that yes, they were flitting. The family unpacked and stayed. A boggart cannot be left behind, only driven out, and a horseshoe over the door is said to help.

water_elemental.name: water elemental
water_elemental.lore: The physician Paracelsus taught that each of the four elements has its own people, and he named the spirits of water undines. This is the element itself, without the manners. It rises from a flooded hall as a standing wave with something like a face, falls on its prey with the weight of a river, and drags it under. Fire means nothing to it. Lightning runs all through it.

air_elemental.name: air elemental
air_elemental.lore: The wind has always had names. The Greeks kept four of them, Boreas, Notus, Eurus and Zephyrus, and said King Aeolus held the rest shut in a cave. Paracelsus called the spirits of the air sylphs. An air elemental is a whirlwind with a will: nearly invisible, quick as a thrown knife, and full of grit and splinters that flay whatever it wraps around.

ice_elemental.name: ice elemental
ice_elemental.lore: The Norse said the world began in ice. Rivers flowing out of Niflheim froze layer upon layer in the great gap, and where sparks from the fire realm met the rime, the frost giant Ymir took shape from the thaw. An ice elemental is a small piece of that first cold, walking. Its touch sheathes a limb in frost. Fire is the one argument it understands.

magma_elemental.name: magma elemental
magma_elemental.lore: The Greeks said Zeus ended his war with the monster Typhon by throwing Mount Etna on top of him, and that the mountain smokes and burns because Typhon is still struggling underneath. A magma elemental is molten rock that has learned to walk. Stone floors glow where it has stepped. Everything it touches burns, and only bitter cold makes it stiffen and crack.

void_elemental.name: void elemental
void_elemental.lore: Before there was earth or sky, the Norse poets said, there was Ginnungagap, the yawning gap: no sand, no sea, no grass, only emptiness between the ice and the fire. A void elemental is a scrap of that emptiness that was never filled. It looks like a hole cut in the air. Light and sound go into it and do not come back out.

shambling_mound.name: shambling mound
shambling_mound.lore: A heap of rotting reeds, creeper and bog moss wound around a living root, walking upright because nothing has told it that it cannot. It smothers what it catches and lets the catch rot into its own bulk. Cold only slows the rot. Lightning wakes it up: a mound struck in a storm rises larger. Fire is what it fears.

assassin_vine.name: assassin vine
assassin_vine.lore: The strangler fig of the tropics sprouts high in another tree, sends roots down around the trunk, and squeezes for years until the host dies and rots away inside a hollow lattice of fig. The assassin vine is in more of a hurry. It lies along a wall like any creeper until something warm brushes past, then loops and tightens. Its roots are well fed.

thorn_slinger.name: thorn slinger
thorn_slinger.lore: A squat, pale shrub that grows where passages narrow. Its seed pods are packed with barbed thorns under pressure, and a footfall nearby is enough to make it fire the lot. The thorns are coated in a sap that burns in the blood. It cannot chase anything. It simply plants itself in a doorway and lets the dungeon's traffic come to it.

myconid_worker.name: myconid worker
myconid_worker.lore: A ring of mushrooms in a meadow was once called a fairy ring, the mark where the fair folk danced. Underground the rings walk. Myconid workers are waist-high mushroom folk who tend the fungus beds of their circle and want only to be left alone. Crowd one, and it puffs a cloud of spores that fills the head with things that are not there.

myconid_sovereign.name: myconid sovereign
myconid_sovereign.lore: A mushroom is only the fruit. The real body is a web of threads running through the soil, and one honey fungus in the mountains of Oregon spreads through miles of forest floor as a single living thing. A myconid sovereign is the heart of such a web. Every mushroom in its caverns is part of it, and it thinks with all of them at once.

yellow_musk_creeper.name: yellow musk creeper
yellow_musk_creeper.lore: The yellow musk creeper produces intoxicating clouds of yellow pollen that overwhelm the minds of victims, drawing them into range of its grasping tendrils. Mindless thralls under its influence protect it and carry decomposing organic matter to fertilize its roots. The musk pollen alone is enough to drive most animals into docile confusion.

gas_spore.name: gas spore
gas_spore.lore: Gas spores are floating fungal pods that superficially resemble beholders, leading to fatal cases of mistaken identity among dungeon veterans. Any puncture causes them to detonate in a cloud of toxic spores. Those slain by the gas spore become hosts for new pods within hours.

violet_fungus.name: violet fungus
violet_fungus.lore: It looks like any other cave mushroom, violet-capped and as tall as a child, until its four ropy branches begin to feel about in the dark. Flesh they touch goes soft and grey, as fruit does around a bruise. It roots where things have died and makes sure the supply continues. Other fungi grow thickly around it and share the spoils.

pegasus_corrupted.name: corrupted pegasus
pegasus_corrupted.lore: Pegasus sprang from the neck of Medusa when Perseus cut off her head. Bellerophon tamed him with a golden bridle given by Athena, and where his hoof struck Mount Helicon the spring of the Muses welled up. This winged horse came of that line. Something in the deep found it and darkened it: its coat has gone the colour of soot, and its hooves leave a chill.

unicorn_corrupted.name: corrupted unicorn
unicorn_corrupted.lore: The old bestiaries say that when a serpent poisons a pool, the animals wait at the edge until the unicorn comes and dips its horn, and the water is made clean. They also say no hunter can take it, only a maiden it trusts. Someone betrayed this one. Its horn has turned black and twisted, and now poisons what it once made pure.

sphinx_lesser.name: lesser sphinx
sphinx_lesser.lore: At Thebes in Egypt an avenue of stone sphinxes more than a mile long joined the temples of Karnak and Luxor, hundreds of them, crouched in two facing rows. They were set there as guardians of the road. A lesser sphinx is a guardian still: lion-bodied, sharp-tongued, and short of patience. It asks its riddle once. A wrong answer, or a slow one, tires it quickly.

nue.name: nue
nue.lore: The Tale of the Heike tells how a black cloud settled over the palace each night and the young Emperor Konoe fell sick with terror. The archer Minamoto no Yorimasa shot into the cloud, and a beast fell out: a monkey's head, a raccoon dog's body, a tiger's legs, a snake for a tail. His retainer I no Hayata finished it. Its cry, like a thrush calling at night, brings bad dreams.

peryton.name: peryton
peryton.lore: Jorge Luis Borges set down the legend: winged stags with the plumage of birds, exiles from drowned Atlantis, each casting the shadow of a man. A peryton gets its own shadow back only by killing a human being, and it can do so once. A sibyl is said to have foretold that they would bring down Rome. This one's shadow still walks on two legs.

carbuncle.name: carbuncle
carbuncle.lore: Spanish explorers in Paraguay swore they had glimpsed it at night: a small animal with a jewel in its forehead that shone like a live coal. The priest Barco Centenera wrote in 1602 that he had hunted it through the forests and never laid hands on one. No one could say what the creature looked like, only the light. The flash dazzles, and then it bites.

sea_dragon_spawn.name: sea dragon spawn
sea_dragon_spawn.lore: When Olaus Magnus drew his great map of the northern seas in 1539, he filled the water off Norway with serpents coiling around ships. Sailors had told him what they saw. A sea dragon's young are hatched in the black trenches and come up flooded rivers into the deep halls. Even half grown, one can crack a hull, and its spat water strikes cold as sleet.

goblin_shaman.name: goblin shaman
goblin_shaman.lore: A goblin shaman is whichever goblin ate the wrong mushroom, survived, and came back talking to things. It wears a mask cut from a giant mushroom cap, shakes a rattle of knucklebones, and stays well behind its kin, screeching orders and curses in the same breath. The hexes are crude. They work anyway, and a warband with a shaman fights twice as boldly as one without.

goblin_king.name: goblin king
goblin_king.lore: Goblins do not inherit crowns. A goblin king takes his by outliving every rival, usually by arranging for someone bigger to do the killing. The crown is bent copper coins wired together with the teeth of the last king. He rules by volume: his shriek carries down three corridors, and every goblin who hears it would sooner face a crusader than face him afterward.

hobgoblin_captain.name: hobgoblin captain
hobgoblin_captain.lore: Where goblins swarm, hobgoblins drill. A captain earned the rank on a battlefield, promoted over the body of the officer before him, and he carries the company banner strapped to his back so the line always knows where to form. He does not charge. He sends two soldiers around the flank, waits until the retreat is cut off, and then advances behind his shield.

hobgoblin_warlord.name: hobgoblin warlord
hobgoblin_warlord.lore: A hobgoblin warlord commands by a soldier's code with one law above the rest: the coward dies first, and by his own captain's hand. Every plate of his armor carries a trophy from an enemy he killed himself, because trophies taken by others do not count. He has read the ground before the fight begins, and his roar turns a wavering line back into a wall.

bugbear.name: bugbear
bugbear.lore: The bugbear lent its name to every nameless dread: in old English a 'bug' was a goblin or bogey, the thing nurses used to frighten children into bed. The real creature is seven feet of fur and muscle that somehow walks without a sound. It likes its prey afraid first. A corridor that has gone suddenly quiet is the only warning it gives.

bugbear_chieftain.name: bugbear chieftain
bugbear_chieftain.lore: A bugbear chieftain holds his territory because every challenger's skull now hangs from his belt, the previous chieftain's among them. Lesser monsters nearby pay him tribute in meat and stay out of his way. He fights with a spiked morningstar and opens with a roar meant to freeze the blood, since a frightened enemy is slower and he is too lazy to chase.

orc_berserker.name: orc berserker
orc_berserker.lore: The word comes from the Norse berserkir, warriors who fought in a trance, bit the rims of their shields, and were said to feel neither fire nor iron. Orc warbands keep the custom. The berserker goes in first, alone and howling, with no shield and no thought of coming back. The rest of the warband follows a few heartbeats later, into whatever gap he has torn.

orc_warchief.name: orc warchief
orc_warchief.lore: No orc is born a warchief. Any warrior in the band may challenge for the title, the fight is to the death, and the winner keeps the loser's hammer. The one who holds it now has answered that challenge many times. Orcs sneer at clever tactics as cowardice, yet a warchief's ambushes are laid with real cunning. He simply calls it hunting.

bandit_captain.name: bandit captain
bandit_captain.lore: A bandit captain was a soldier once, and decided the pay was better on the other side of the law. He has claimed a stretch of corridor as a toll road and collects in coin or in blood. There is nothing showy in how he fights: he picks out the most dangerous opponent, puts a thrown dagger into him first, and closes with the sword.

dark_cultist.name: dark cultist
dark_cultist.lore: A dark cultist gave up a name, a family, and a trade to serve something that whispers from below. The little ritual he has learned is enough to make a prayer bite like a blade, and his knife carries a curse that clouds the eyes. He hunts relics for his master and counts his own life a small price. Holy things burn him, and he knows it.

mercenary_veteran.name: mercenary veteran
mercenary_veteran.lore: The veteran has outlived three paymasters and most of his company. He holds no cause and no grudge: someone down here pays in gold, so here he stands. His sword is plain and his shield is dented, but he has spent thirty years learning exactly where a guard opens. He will not waste a stroke, and he will not chase a fight he cannot win.

battle_mage.name: battle mage
battle_mage.lore: A battle mage has thrown away nine tenths of the wizard's art to make the last tenth fast. The tattoos running down both arms are channels, inked so that fire or frost can leave the hand in the time it takes to point. The inking hurts, and so does every casting. He wears little armor and keeps his distance, because up close he is only a scholar with sore arms.

hill_giant.name: hill giant
hill_giant.lore: Hill giants are the smallest and dullest of giantkind, which still leaves them twice the height of a tall man and able to throw a boulder the size of a barrel. They den in caverns, eat whatever they catch, and keep hoards sorted by no rule except shiny, big, or edible. A hill giant rarely means malice. It is simply always hungry.

stone_giant.name: stone giant
stone_giant.lore: Stone giants are grey as the rock they live in, and can stand so still that travelers walk past them as part of the wall. They are carvers: whole galleries of the deep caverns are covered in their slow, patient reliefs. They hold the sunlit world in contempt and treat anyone who climbs down from it as a trespasser, to be answered with a thrown boulder.

cloud_giant.name: cloud giant
cloud_giant.lore: Jack climbed his beanstalk to a giant's castle in the sky, and the old tale had the right of it. Cloud giants keep their halls on the storm-heads and look down, in every sense, on the folk below. The few found underground are exiles or treasure seekers after some ancient prize. They are too proud to bother with small creatures until one gets in the way.

storm_giant.name: storm giant
storm_giant.lore: Storm giants are the greatest of giantkind, and they keep the weather the way lesser lords keep hounds. Each swing of a storm giant's sword arrives with thunder attached. They live so long that they remember when these halls were first dug, and they speak of it as recent. What one wants in the deep is its own affair. It is unwise to ask twice.

cyclops_brute.name: cyclops brute
cyclops_brute.lore: Odysseus met the most famous of this race: Polyphemus, a shepherd who ate six of his crew and was blinded with a sharpened olive stake while he slept off the wine. The brutes below keep no flocks and have no such manners. One eye judges distance poorly, so their thrown boulders often miss. Their fists, at arm's length, do not.

two_headed_ogre.name: two-headed ogre
two_headed_ogre.lore: Two heads share one body and agree on nothing: which way to walk, whose turn it is to sleep, who gets the first bite. The quarrel stops the moment something edible walks in. Then each head takes charge of one arm and one club, and the creature that could not decide on supper fights like two ogres standing in the same place. One head always keeps watch.

ice_troll.name: ice troll
ice_troll.lore: Norse trolls were creatures of the mountain and the frost, and this breed has kept to the cold. It haunts the flooded caverns where meltwater runs in from the glaciers. Cut flesh closes again while the swordsman watches, and its claws leave frostbite where they land. Fire is the old answer to a troll and remains the right one: a burned wound stays burned.

drow_warrior.name: drow warrior
drow_warrior.lore: The dark elves trained this one from the cradle, in cities that have never seen the sun. The blade is short, light, and beautifully made. The weapon to fear is the little crossbow in the off hand: its bolts are tipped with a sleeping venom, because the dark elves want prisoners for their mines and altars far more than they want corpses.

drow_mage.name: drow mage
drow_mage.lore: In a city with no daylight, shadow is not the absence of something. It is the raw material. Dark elf mages spend centuries learning to shape it into bolts that blind, and into drifting pale fires that cling to an enemy and muddle the wits. Their spellbooks are written in silver ink on black pages, and surface scholars pay dearly for one.

drow_priestess.name: drow priestess
drow_priestess.lore: Among the dark elves the priestesses rule and everyone else obeys. This one serves a spider goddess who rewards treachery and punishes failure, and she carries a whip whose lashes are living snakes. Her blessing can lift a household to power in a season. Her curse can end a bloodline in a night. She has used both, and enjoyed the second more.

minotaur_warrior.name: minotaur warrior
minotaur_warrior.lore: The first Minotaur was a prisoner of the Labyrinth. His descendants have made the maze a fortress. A minotaur warrior never loses his way underground, and he uses that gift without mercy: he retreats down a side passage, circles, and comes back from behind. He fights with a double axe in the Cretan fashion and finishes with his horns.

young_black_dragon.name: young black dragon
young_black_dragon.lore: Black dragons lair in swamps and drowned cellars, and they spit acid where their cousins breathe fire. Even a young one has the full measure of the family's spite. It likes to hold prey under water until the struggling stops, then leave the meal to soften. Already it is counting coins: a hoard has to start somewhere, and an adventurer's purse will do.

young_red_dragon.name: young red dragon
young_red_dragon.lore: Red dragons believe that everything under the sky is theirs and merely on loan to others. A young one has all of that pride and only some of the size. The lair runs hot enough to feel from two rooms away, and the stone near its bed has melted and set again like wax. It expects tribute. Failing that, it takes it.

adult_blue_dragon.name: adult blue dragon
adult_blue_dragon.lore: Blue dragons love order, though not justice. An adult keeps a web of servants, spies, and tributaries, each in an assigned place, and it treats a disturbance in that arrangement as a personal insult. Its breath is lightning, a single white stroke that leaps from one armored body to the next. It plans its battles, and it has already planned this one.

adult_red_dragon.name: adult red dragon
adult_red_dragon.lore: Greed, pride, and cruelty, grown to full size. An adult red dragon has spent centuries stripping the lands around it, and it sleeps on the result: a bed of coin and plate deep enough to drown in. It knows every piece. The dragon in Beowulf burned a kingdom over one stolen cup, and this one would do the same without a second thought.

drake_fire.name: fire drake
drake_fire.lore: A fire drake is a dragon's poor relation: four legs, a furnace in the belly, and no more wit than a mastiff. It hunts, eats, and sleeps on whatever glitters. Its spit is a gobbet of burning pitch, far short of a true dragon's breath, but it will set a cloak or a rope bridge alight. Stronger monsters keep drakes as watchdogs and feed them the trespassers.

drake_cold.name: frost drake
drake_cold.lore: Frost drakes keep to the deep levels where the glaciers press in, and the rime never melts off their scales. They cling to the ceiling above a passage and breathe down a freezing fog, then drop on whatever has stopped moving. The lair is easy to find. The walls are glazed with ice, and last month's meals stand in it like flies in amber.

yuan_ti_pureblood.name: yuan-ti pureblood
yuan_ti_pureblood.lore: The serpent folk worship a snake god that died long ago, and its death has not troubled their faith at all. The ones called purebloods pass for human at a glance. Only a patch of scales at the neck or a slow, unblinking stare gives them away. They join caravans and delving parties as guides, and report every word back to the temple.

wyvern_greater.name: greater wyvern
wyvern_greater.lore: Heralds know the wyvern well: two legs, two wings, and a barbed tail, where a true dragon has four legs. It has no breath weapon and does not miss one. A greater wyvern's wings can fill a corridor from wall to wall, and the sting at the end of its tail swings over its back like a scorpion's, carrying venom enough to stop a horse's heart.

naga_guardian.name: naga guardian
naga_guardian.lore: In the old stories of India the nagas are serpent lords who guard treasure and sacred waters, hooded like cobras and wise as kings. Someone set this one over a vault or a tomb centuries ago, and it has not left its post since. It knows every stone of the place. It regards a stranger there much as a householder regards a thief.

shadow_master.name: shadow master
shadow_master.lore: A common shadow is hunger without a mind. A shadow master has drained enough of the living to remember, dimly and wrongly, that it once had a name. The memory makes it patient. It slides along the unlit side of a corridor like a fish through water and strikes from behind, and its touch takes strength and warmth together. Torchlight and holy things drive it back.

void_crawler.name: void crawler
void_crawler.lore: Where great magic has worn the world thin, things come through. The void crawler is one: a many-limbed shape that is never entirely present, so that a sword passes through an arm that was there a moment ago. Being near it bends the senses. Those it touches see doors that are not there and friends who are. It feeds while they stare.

ruinous_djinn.name: ruinous djinn
ruinous_djinn.lore: The old Arabian accounts say the jinn were made from smokeless fire, and the tales add that King Solomon sealed the rebellious ones in brass vessels and cast them into the sea. This one spent its centuries in the bottle going mad. It is free now and has no home to return to, so it breaks things: walls, doors, chains, and anyone who reminds it of a jailer.

undead_colossus.name: undead colossus
undead_colossus.lore: A necromancer needed a wall knocked down and had the corpses of giants to hand. The result is a colossus: dead giants' limbs stitched together with ship's cable and held by binding runes burned into the hide. No care went into it. It was made to be used up. It has no thoughts at all and carries out the last order it was given, forever.

elder_werewolf.name: elder werewolf
elder_werewolf.lore: Petronius told of a soldier who turned wolf among the tombstones, and the Greeks said King Lycaon was the first, cursed by Zeus. This one has changed so many times that the man no longer comes back. It leads a pack with a soldier's cunning and bites for the hamstring. A wound from ordinary steel closes behind the blade. A wound from silver does not.

abyssal_champion.name: abyssal champion
abyssal_champion.lore: A demon earns the title of champion by killing: a thousand mortal warriors, each one counted, each one's weapon kept. It hunts skilled fighters on purpose, because a title built on easy victims is worth nothing in the Abyss. Its sword burns with hellfire and it salutes before it strikes. The courtesy is mockery. It has never yet met the opponent it was looking for.

bone_titan.name: bone titan
bone_titan.lore: Several giants' skeletons went into this one, wired together bone on bone until the skull scrapes a thirty-foot ceiling. The floor shakes when it walks. A necromancer who can raise such a thing does not waste it on one doorway: a bone titan holds a whole wing of the dungeon. Blades skitter off its ribs. A heavy hammer, patiently applied, takes it apart.

spectral_lord.name: spectral lord
spectral_lord.lore: Some of the dead refuse to go. The spectral lord was a warlord or an archmage whose ambition outlasted the body, and it has had centuries to brood. It still wears the shape of its armor or robes, drawn in pale light. Steel passes through it like smoke. Its wail carries the despair of the grave, and it holds the living in the same contempt it always did.

chaos_troll.name: chaos troll
chaos_troll.lore: Trolls heal. This one lived too close to a rift, and now it heals wrong. A severed arm grows back as two; a split skull closes around a second face that looks the other way. Each wound leaves it larger and less sane, and its claws carry the same disorder into the mind. Fire and acid seal the flesh. Nothing else slows it.

wyrm.name: wyrm
wyrm.lore: Wyrm is the oldest English word for a dragon: the Beowulf poet used it for the hoard-guarder that killed his hero. The name fits the old, heavy kind found here, a serpent grown too vast to fly, dragging its belly along tunnels it has worn smooth. It has been breathing fire since before these halls had doors, and it has only grown better at it.

elder_mind_flayer.name: elder mind flayer
elder_mind_flayer.lore: It has the body of a robed man and the head of an octopus, and it eats minds. This one has fed for centuries on scholars, generals, and kings, and kept what they knew. Its thought strikes like a hammer and leaves the victim unsure of the last hour. It considers fighting beneath it. If it is fighting, something has already made it very angry.

void_leviathan.name: void leviathan
void_leviathan.lore: The Leviathan of the Book of Job was a sea beast no hook could hold. This thing is larger and comes from no sea: it swims in the dark between worlds and squeezes through wherever magic has torn a hole. Parts of its length are always elsewhere, so no chain or ward can bind it. It is drawn to warmth and swallows whatever gives it off.

elder_beholder.name: elder beholder
elder_beholder.lore: A floating orb of flesh with one great central eye, a mouth full of teeth, and a crown of lesser eyes on stalks, each one a different way to die. An elder has grown extra stalks with age and learned to use them all at once. It trusts nothing and forgets nothing. Somewhere in its lair is a careful list of everything it has ever met, sorted by danger and by flavor.

dread_wyrm.name: dread wyrm
dread_wyrm.lore: Something poisoned this dragon while it was still growing. Its body kept the bulk of a great wyrm and its mind kept the temper of a hatchling, and neither ever finished. It knows what it should have been, and the knowledge has soured into a rage that burns hotter than a healthy dragon's fire. It cannot be bargained with. Nobody has found anything it wants more than revenge.

abyssal_overlord.name: abyssal overlord
abyssal_overlord.lore: An overlord rules a whole layer of the Abyss, a country of fire and screaming where lesser demons fight each other for eternity because nothing else is permitted. When it climbs into the mortal world it brings that country with it. Stone runs like wax around its feet, and directions stop meaning anything. Holy ground is the one thing that does not bend.

elder_dragon.name: elder dragon
elder_dragon.lore: Five hundred years is middle age for a dragon. An elder has outgrown the rashness of youth and has not yet settled into the long sleep of the truly ancient, which makes this the most dangerous season of its life. It can level a town in an afternoon and has the sense to pick the afternoon. Its hoard is old enough to hold the coins of forgotten kings.

lich_sovereign.name: lich sovereign
lich_sovereign.lore: A king who would not die, and found a way. The lich sovereign hid its soul in a phylactery buried under the ruins of its old capital, and it rules the dead here exactly as it once ruled the living: with ledgers. Every intruder is recorded, assessed, and assigned a manner of disposal. The crown is still on the skull. The court still bows.

demon_emperor.name: demon emperor
demon_emperor.lore: There are many lords in Hell and they are never at peace. An emperor holds its throne by ceaseless war on its rivals and on the mortal world alike, and by schemes laid across centuries. The title has one fixed requirement: the claimant must have destroyed a civilization with its own hands. It lists this among its honors, the way a knight lists a tournament.

world_serpent.name: world serpent
world_serpent.lore: The Norse told of a serpent that Odin threw into the sea, which grew until it circled the whole world and bit its own tail. The coils that fill these halls are of that kind, lying where the foundations of the earth are laid bare. They are older than any kingdom above. Scales turn a sword as a cliff turns rain, and when one shifts in its sleep, the ground shakes.

entropy_wraith.name: entropy wraith
entropy_wraith.lore: Leave a wraith long enough and it wears through. The entropy wraith is what remains: a hole in the shape of a ghost, with nothing behind it. It bears no malice, for it has forgotten how. Things near it simply come apart: mortar from stone, color from cloth, memory from the mind. What follows it is older than death, the emptiness before the first day.

asterion_minotaur.name: Asterion the Minotaur
asterion_minotaur.lore: Asterion, 'the starry one', was born to Queen Pasiphae and the white bull of Poseidon. King Minos hid his shame in the Labyrinth that Daedalus built, and fed it with seven youths and seven maidens sent from Athens as tribute. Theseus ended the tribute and found his way back out by Ariadne's thread. Down here a thread is harder to come by, and the bull-headed prince is still hungry.
asterion_minotaur.enrage_message: Asterion lowers his horns and comes on. There will be no more hiding in the walls.

medusa_gorgon.name: Medusa the Gorgon
medusa_gorgon.lore: Ovid says Medusa was a mortal beauty whom Athena cursed: her hair became living snakes, and whoever met her eyes turned to stone. Perseus came for her with a polished bronze shield, watched only her reflection, and struck off her head with a curved blade. The winged horse Pegasus sprang from her blood. Her garden of statues grows larger every year.

fafnir_dragon.name: Fafnir the Dragon
fafnir_dragon.lore: Fafnir was a dwarf who murdered his father Hreidmar for the cursed gold of Andvari, then lay down on it and became a dragon. His breath poisoned the heath around him and his scales turned every edge. Sigurd dug a pit in the track Fafnir used on his way to drink, and drove the sword Gram up through the soft belly as the dragon crawled overhead.

fenrir_wolf.name: Fenrir, Wolf of Ragnarok
fenrir_wolf.lore: Fenrir is the wolf-son of Loki. The gods bound him with Gleipnir, a ribbon the dwarves made from six things that do not exist, among them the sound of a cat's footfall and the roots of a mountain. He would allow it only if a god laid a hand in his jaws as a pledge. Tyr did, and lost the hand. At Ragnarok the wolf swallows Odin.

abaddon_destroyer.name: Abaddon the Destroyer
abaddon_destroyer.lore: Revelation names him twice: Abaddon in Hebrew, Apollyon in Greek, and both mean the Destroyer. He is the angel of the bottomless pit and king over the locusts that pour from it when the fifth trumpet sounds, with faces like men, teeth like lions, and tails that sting like scorpions. This is the last floor. Beyond him there is nothing left to descend to.

arachne.name: Arachne
arachne.lore: Arachne of Lydia wove so well that she challenged Athena, and Ovid admits the goddess could find no flaw in her work. Worse, the tapestry showed the gods' own misdeeds. Athena tore it apart and struck her with the shuttle, and Arachne was changed into a spider, to hang and spin forever. Her thread is still perfect, and she still resents a critic.
arachne.omen: Every doorway on this floor has been measured for a web.

talos.name: Talos
talos.lore: Hephaestus forged Talos of bronze to guard Crete, and the giant ran around the island three times a day, hurling rocks at any ship that came near. One vein ran from his neck to his ankle, closed with a single bronze nail. When the Argonauts arrived, Medea bewitched him, the nail came out, and his ichor poured away like molten lead.
talos.omen: The floor is warm in a path that circles the level, as if something heavy walks its rounds.

echidna.name: Echidna
echidna.lore: Hesiod calls Echidna half fair-cheeked nymph and half speckled serpent, living in a cave beneath the earth where she never grows old. By Typhon she bore the worst brood in Greek myth: Cerberus, the Lernaean Hydra, the Chimera, and the two-headed hound Orthrus. Most of her children fell to Heracles. The mother of monsters is still down here, and still nesting.
echidna.omen: The walls here are scored with claw marks of a dozen different shapes.

erlking.name: Erlking
erlking.lore: Goethe's ballad tells it: a father rides hard through the night with his feverish son in his arms. The boy sees a crowned figure in the mist who whispers of games and golden robes. The father sees only fog and willows. When they reach home, the child is dead. The Erlking still makes his offers in a soft voice, and cold iron still spoils his mood.
erlking.omen: A child's voice calls from the dark, and then a man's, sweetly, in answer.

camazotz.name: Camazotz
camazotz.lore: In the Popol Vuh of the K'iche' Maya, the Hero Twins must spend a night in the House of Bats in Xibalba. They hid inside their blowguns. Hunahpu put his head out to see whether dawn had come, and Camazotz, the death bat, took it off at the neck. The lords of the underworld hung the head in their ball court. He has come hunting another.
camazotz.omen: Something large shifts on the ceiling, out of the light, and is still.

cacus.name: Cacus
cacus.lore: Virgil's Cacus was a fire-breathing son of Vulcan who lived in a cave on the Aventine Hill, its doorway hung with the heads of his victims. He stole cattle from Hercules and dragged them in by their tails, so the tracks would point the wrong way. Their lowing betrayed him. Hercules tore the roof off the hill, plunged through the smoke, and strangled him.
cacus.omen: Hoof prints in the dust lead backwards, away from where the cattle went.

the_sphinx.name: The Sphinx
the_sphinx.lore: The Sphinx of Thebes had a woman's face, a lion's body, and an eagle's wings. She sat on a rock above the road and asked each traveler what goes on four legs at morning, two at noon, and three at evening, and she ate the ones who could not say. When Oedipus answered her, she threw herself from the cliff. She has learned harder riddles since.
the_sphinx.omen: Answers are scratched into the wall here. Every one of them is crossed out.

rangda.name: Rangda
rangda.lore: On Bali, Rangda is the widow-witch: wild white hair, tusks, and a tongue that hangs to her waist. She commands the leyaks, sorcerers who fly by night, and she fights an unending duel with Barong, the lion-like guardian of the villages. In the temple dance her spell turns the warriors' own daggers against them. Neither side ever wins, and the dance begins again.
rangda.omen: Offerings of rice and flowers lie rotting at every corner of this floor.

nemean_lion.name: Nemean Lion
nemean_lion.lore: The first labor of Hercules. His arrows bounced off the Nemean Lion's golden hide and his sword bent on it, so he drove the beast into its cave, blocked one of the two entrances, and choked it to death with his bare arms. Only the lion's own claws could cut the pelt, which he wore ever after. Edges are wasted on it. A crushing blow is not.
nemean_lion.omen: A broken sword lies by the stairs, bent double. There is no blood on it.

baba_yaga.name: Baba Yaga
baba_yaga.lore: Baba Yaga's hut stands on chicken legs behind a fence of bones, topped with skulls whose eyes glow at night. She flies in a mortar, rowing with the pestle and sweeping away her trail with a broom. Her teeth are iron. In the Russian tales she sometimes helps a hero who is polite and finishes her tasks, as Vasilisa did. The rude ones go in the oven.
baba_yaga.omen: The floor is swept clean in one long line, as if by a broom.

jormungandr_juvenile.name: Jörmungandr (Juvenile)
jormungandr_juvenile.lore: Odin threw Loki's serpent child into the sea, where it grew until it circled Midgard and took its own tail in its mouth. Thor once hooked it using an ox head for bait, and the giant Hymir cut the line in terror. At Ragnarok Thor kills it at last, walks nine steps, and falls dead of its venom. This is a young one. The venom is the same.
jormungandr_juvenile.omen: A dry riverbed crosses this floor. It is a slough, and it is fresh.

sets_jackal.name: Set's Jackal
sets_jackal.lore: Set murdered his brother Osiris, scattered the pieces across Egypt, and fought Horus for the throne through eighty years of trials. He is lord of the red desert, of storms, and of strangers. Anubis, the jackal who weighs hearts, guides the dead with care. Set's jackals are his dark reflection: they come up out of the desert night and hunt the living for sport.
sets_jackal.omen: Red sand has drifted against the walls, though there is no desert for a hundred floors.

green_knight.name: The Green Knight
green_knight.lore: On New Year's Day a giant knight, green from hair to horse, rode into Camelot and offered his own axe to anyone who would trade blow for blow. Gawain struck off his head. The knight picked it up, reminded Gawain of his appointment in a year's time, and rode out. He was Sir Bertilak, enchanted by Morgan le Fay, and he keeps his bargains exactly.
green_knight.omen: Holly grows from the bare stone here, in full berry.
green_knight.revive_message: The Green Knight stoops, lifts his head by the hair, and sets it back on his shoulders. "Now it is my turn."

charybdis.name: Charybdis
charybdis.lore: Three times a day Charybdis swallows the sea and three times spits it back, and the strait opposite Scylla's cliff boils like a cauldron. Circe told Odysseus to steer for Scylla and lose six men sooner than lose the ship. Later, alone on a raft, he was drawn in anyway, and saved himself by hanging from a fig tree over her mouth until the timbers came back up.
charybdis.omen: The puddles on this floor all lean the same way.

ravanas_arm.name: Ravana's Arm
ravanas_arm.lore: Ravana, king of Lanka, had ten heads and twenty arms, and he carried off Sita, the wife of Rama. In the war that followed, Rama's arrows struck off his heads and each one grew back, until a weapon given by the gods found his heart. This arm did not die with him. It drags itself along by its fingers, and it still has a king's grip.
ravanas_arm.omen: Five long furrows are gouged into the floor, side by side, wider than a doorway.

wendigo.name: Wendigo
wendigo.lore: The Algonquian peoples of the northern forests tell of the wendigo: a gaunt giant with a heart of ice, born when a starving person eats human flesh in the dead of winter. It grows with every meal, so its hunger always outruns its feeding, and it is never full. Cold walks ahead of it. Fire is what the old stories use to melt the heart.
wendigo.omen: It is colder here than it should be, and you are hungrier than you were on the stair.

wild_hunt_captain.name: Wild Hunt Captain
wild_hunt_captain.lore: On winter nights, all across the north, people heard hounds and horns in the sky and barred their doors. The Germans said Wotan led the riders; the English said Herne the Hunter, or old King Herla, who cannot dismount. To see the Hunt was an omen of death. To be caught in its path was to ride with it. The captain's horn has already sounded.
wild_hunt_captain.omen: A horn sounds, very far off, and then not so far.

anansi.name: Anansi
anansi.lore: Anansi the spider wanted the stories of the world, and Nyame the Sky God named a price no one could pay: Onini the python, Osebo the leopard, the Mmoboro hornets, and a fairy no one could see. Anansi caught all four by talk and trickery, and since then the Akan call every tale a spider story. He does not fight fair. He does not need to.
anansi.omen: A thread crosses the stair at ankle height. It hums when you step over it.

nidhoggr_fragment.name: Níðhöggr Fragment
nidhoggr_fragment.lore: Níðhöggr lies beneath the root of Yggdrasil that reaches the spring Hvergelmir, and gnaws. The squirrel Ratatoskr runs up and down the trunk carrying insults between the dragon and the eagle at the top. The seeress of the Voluspa sees him still flying after Ragnarok, with corpses under his wings. Even a piece of him is patient enough to chew through anything.
nidhoggr_fragment.omen: Roots as thick as pillars come down through the ceiling. Something has been gnawing them.

seal_demon_wrath.name: Amon, Demon of Wrath
seal_demon_wrath.lore: The old grimoires list Amon as a Marquis of Hell: a wolf with a serpent's tail who vomits flame, commanding forty legions. He stirs up feuds and, when it suits him, mends them. Abaddon set him at the First Seal because nothing kept in anger ever leaves willingly. His body smolders like a banked forge and his fists come down white-hot.
seal_demon_wrath.enrage_message: Amon's flame goes from red to white. He has stopped holding anything back.
rage_messages: The air round Amon is too hot to breathe.

seal_demon_pestilence.name: Buer, Demon of Pestilence
seal_demon_pestilence.lore: Buer is a President of Hell with fifty legions under him. The grimoires say he teaches philosophy and the virtues of every herb, and an old engraving shows him as a lion's head ringed by five goat legs, rolling like a wheel. The physician's knowledge runs both ways. He knows which leaf cures a fever, and so he knows which one starts it. He guards the Second Seal.

seal_demon_famine.name: Mammon, Demon of Famine
seal_demon_famine.lore: The Gospel warns that no one can serve both God and mammon, and the Aramaic word simply means wealth. Medieval writers made Mammon a prince of Hell, the demon of avarice. He guards the Third Seal as famine, which is greed's other face: the granary locked while the village starves. Bread goes stale near him and strength leaves the arms. He is never satisfied.

seal_demon_war.name: Bael, Demon of War
seal_demon_war.lore: The Lesser Key of Solomon names Bael first among the kings of Hell: ruler of the east, master of sixty-six legions, appearing with the heads of a man, a toad, and a cat. He speaks in a hoarse voice and can teach a man to walk unseen. He holds the Fourth Seal in iron plate hammered from the swords of the fallen, and he has never yielded a field.

seal_demon_death.name: Samael, Demon of Death
seal_demon_death.lore: Samael's name means the Venom of God. In the old rabbinic tales he is the angel of death, who stands at the bedside with a drop of gall on the point of his sword. Tradition never quite settled whether he fell. Abaddon has settled it for him and bound him to the Fifth Seal. His touch is the cold of a grave dug for someone in particular.

seal_demon_earthquake.name: Beleth, Demon of the Earthquake
seal_demon_earthquake.lore: Beleth is a king of Hell who rides a pale horse, with trumpets sounding before him and eighty-five legions behind. The grimoires warn that he arrives in a fury. Revelation says that when the Sixth Seal opens there is a great earthquake, the sun turns black as sackcloth, and the moon becomes like blood. Beleth carries that hour with him, and the floor splits where his horse treads.

seal_demon_silence.name: Abyzou, Demon of Silence
seal_demon_silence.lore: The Testament of Solomon tells of Abyzou, a demon who never sleeps and wanders the world out of envy. Solomon had her hung by her hair before the Temple. Revelation says that when the Seventh Seal opened, there was silence in heaven for about half an hour. She keeps that seal now. Prayers and spells alike die unspoken in the stillness around her.

abyssal_locust.name: abyssal locust
abyssal_locust.lore: John saw them rise out of the smoke of the pit: locusts shaped like horses armed for battle, with faces like men, hair like women, teeth like lions, and wings that sounded like chariots charging. They were told to harm no green thing, only people. Their king is Abaddon. One is a pest. They do not come one at a time.

heavenly_angel.name: heavenly angel
heavenly_angel.lore: An angel of the heavenly host, called down by the Scales of Michael. It comes in a column of white light and wastes no word and no motion. It has one errand: to meet the locusts of the pit, one for one, and burn them out of the world. Where angel and locust touch, both vanish in holy fire, and the air smells of rain.

hell_bovine.name: Hell Bovine
hell_bovine.lore: Somewhere beyond the veil there is a pasture where the grass is ash and the herd walks upright. A hell bovine stands as tall as a man, grips a rough halberd in both front hooves, and uses it better than a creature without thumbs has any right to. It lowers its horns before it charges. Nobody knows what the herd wants. It only ever says one thing. Moo.

cow_king.name: Cow King
cow_king.lore: The herd has a king. His horns are gilded, his cape was once royal purple, and he rules the hell bovines of the secret pasture with an iron hoof. Rumor among adventurers holds that killing him brings terrible luck, and that everyone does it anyway. He leads the stampede from the front, and the ground shakes before he arrives. Moo.

skeleton_champion.name: skeleton champion
skeleton_champion.lore: Some warriors drilled so long that the lessons sank into the bone. Dead, raised, and stripped of everything else, a skeleton champion still has every parry and cut it ever learned, and no fear or fatigue to spoil them. Arrows rattle through its ribs. A mace is the proper tool: bone that will not bleed will still break.

dire_wolf_alpha.name: dire wolf alpha
dire_wolf_alpha.lore: The dire wolf was real: heavier than any wolf alive, with jaws built to crack bone. Thousands of them went down in the tar pits of La Brea, lured by trapped prey. Down here the breed never died out. The alpha stands as high as a pony at the shoulder and leads its pack through the deep tunnels by scent, in the dark, in silence.

troll_brute.name: troll brute
troll_brute.lore: Bigger than a common troll and a good deal stupider, the brute has only one idea in a fight, and it is a heavy one. It heals faster than its smaller cousins: a gash closes in moments, and a lost hand is back within the hour. Fire and acid are the only wounds it cannot mend. It has learned to fear a torch, and little else.

elder_basilisk.name: elder basilisk
elder_basilisk.lore: Pliny wrote that the basilisk is king of serpents, crowned with a white mark, and so venomous that when a horseman speared one the poison ran up the lance and killed both rider and horse. This old one has grown to the size of an ox. The limbs it bites stiffen and turn grey, and its lair is ringed with statues that were never carved.

greater_earth_elemental.name: greater earth elemental
greater_earth_elemental.lore: Summoned from the deepest strata, where the rock has never seen light, it rises out of the floor in the rough shape of a man: boulders for fists, a slab for a chest, gravel grinding in every joint. Swords chip on it and lightning runs harmlessly to ground. Miners know the answer. What a pick and a sledge can do to a quarry face, they can do to this.

fungal_horror.name: fungal horror
fungal_horror.lore: It began as a patch of mold on a dead adventurer, and it has been feeding and spreading ever since.
