Now the colony fills a chamber, thinks slow thoughts, and can move when it wishes. It breathes out clouds of spores that sicken the lungs, then settles over whatever falls and digests it at leisure. Like any dry growth, it burns well.

corrosive_ooze.name: corrosive ooze
corrosive_ooze.lore: A heap of grey-green slime that hisses where it touches the floor. It eats metal first: a sword left in it for a few breaths comes out pitted and thin, and mail fares no better. It has no eyes, no front, and no fear, and simply flows toward warmth. Veterans fight it with torches, or with something they do not mind losing.

orc_warlord.name: orc warlord
orc_warlord.lore: A warchief leads a warband. A warlord leads the horde: every band and every chief, sworn to one banner by fear and by plunder. He has been in hundreds of fights and carries a scar from most of them. His armor was forged from the melted weapons of enemies he killed, and each new victory adds a plate. His war cry sets ten thousand feet marching.

veteran_knight.name: veteran knight
veteran_knight.lore: He took his vows young and has kept perhaps half of them. Thirty years of campaigning have left him with masterwork plate, a sword arm that does not tire, and no illusions. Everyone he rode out with is dead. Edges slide off the armor, and he lets them, saving his own strokes for the gaps in other men's. A hammer worries him more than a blade.

greater_fire_elemental.name: greater fire elemental
greater_fire_elemental.lore: A pillar of living flame, twice a man's height, with a core as white as a forge at full blast. Stone slumps and runs where it stands for long. Blades pass through it and come out glowing, having cut nothing. It does not hate. It burns, because that is the whole of what it is, and cold and water are the only things that diminish it.

chimera_alpha.name: chimera alpha
chimera_alpha.lore: Homer describes her: lion in front, serpent behind, a goat in the middle, breathing terrible fire. Bellerophon killed the first Chimera from the back of Pegasus, some say by lodging a lump of lead in her throat so that her own flame melted it. This one has lived long enough to grow huge, and its heads have learned to take turns.

bone_colossus.name: bone colossus
bone_colossus.lore: Hundreds of dead soldiers went into it. The necromancer did not sort them: skulls serve as knuckles, shinbones as fingers, and whole ribcages are packed into the chest like kindling. It walks with a sound like hail on a roof, and small bones shake loose with every step. It flings these too. Hammers undo the work that spears and arrows cannot.

demon_knight.name: demon knight
demon_knight.lore: He was a paladin once. He knelt in the wrong chapel on the worst night of his life and rose with hellfire running down his blade. All the training is still there: the footwork, the guard, the patience behind the shield. Only the faith is gone, and he has replaced it with hatred of anyone who kept theirs. Holy water blisters his armor.

gelatinous_titan.name: gelatinous titan
gelatinous_titan.lore: A gelatinous cube is a clear, quivering block that sweeps a corridor clean of everything living. This one has eaten for so long that it fills the passage from wall to wall and floor to ceiling, and old swords and skeletons hang suspended inside it like fruit in aspic. It is nearly invisible until it is very close. What it touches goes numb, then dissolves.

phase_spider_matriarch.name: phase spider matriarch
phase_spider_matriarch.lore: Ordinary spiders hunt in three dimensions. The phase spider uses a fourth: it steps out of the world, walks around its prey unseen, and steps back in behind it with fangs already bared. The matriarch has been doing this for centuries and has hung her webs on both sides of the veil. Her venom works quickly. Fire clears her silk and drives her off.

manticore_elder.name: manticore elder
manticore_elder.lore: The name is old Persian for man-eater. Ctesias, a Greek physician at the Persian court, described it: a lion's body the color of cinnabar, a man's face with three rows of teeth, and a tail that shoots spines like arrows. An elder's tail bristles with dozens, and each one grows back. It prefers to kill from a distance and eat up close.

war_troll.name: war troll
war_troll.lore: Someone had the idea of putting trolls in an army. War trolls are bred for size, drilled until they will hold a line, and armored in iron plates bolted straight through the hide, since the flesh heals around the bolts overnight. They carry clubs studded with nails. A troll that ordinary wounds cannot kill makes a fine soldier, so long as nobody on the field has fire.

frost_giant_jarl.name: frost giant jarl
frost_giant_jarl.lore: The Norse knew the frost giants as the jotnar of Jotunheim, sprung from the ice-giant Ymir and at war with the gods since the world began. A jarl is a chieftain among them, lord of a hall and a war band. His mail is blue-black glacial iron, his beard is hung with icicles, and the edge of his great axe smokes with a cold that kills what it cuts.

fire_giant_king.name: fire giant king
fire_giant_king.lore: In the Norse telling, Surtr rules Muspelheim, the land of fire, and at Ragnarok he will burn the world with a sword brighter than the sun. The fire giant king is of that kindred. He holds court at a forge beside the magma, and his skin has baked as dark and hard as slag. His hammer never cools. Neither does his breath.

elder_vampire.name: elder vampire
elder_vampire.lore: The word vampire reached English in the 1730s, carried by Austrian army reports from Serbian villages where officers dug up the dead and found them ruddy and unspoiled. This one is far older than those reports. It keeps the manners of a court that no longer exists, and it feeds with the patience of a creature that has outlasted every hunter sent after it.

death_knight_lord.name: death knight lord
death_knight_lord.lore: A commander who broke his oath and was denied his grave. He drills in the dark as he drilled in life, sword strokes exact, armor kept in parade order over nothing but bone. The cold that comes off his blade is the cold of the tomb he should be lying in. He does not hate the living. He simply has standing orders.

arcane_golem.name: arcane golem
arcane_golem.lore: Jewish legend says Rabbi Loew of Prague shaped a man from river clay and woke it with a holy word, and that rubbing out one letter turned 'truth' into 'dead' and stopped it. Some later maker copied the method and none of the reverence. The script covering this golem glows when it strikes, and no one living remembers which letter to erase.

abyssal_hound.name: abyssal hound
abyssal_hound.lore: Hunting dogs of the pit, long in the leg and black as a burnt beam, with embers showing between their teeth. They run in packs and work a quarry the way wolves work an elk: one in front to hold its eyes, the rest at the flanks. Their bite carries hellfire. Cold and consecrated ground are the only things that turn them.

dread_sphinx.name: dread sphinx
dread_sphinx.lore: The Sphinx of Thebes sat on a rock outside the city and strangled every traveler who failed her riddle, until Oedipus answered 'Man' and she threw herself from the cliff. This one took the lesson differently. It no longer waits for an answer. Its riddles lodge in the mind like burrs and leave the listener unsure of his own name, and then the lion's claws do the rest.

lich_lord.name: lich lord
lich_lord.lore: Russian tales tell of Koschei the Deathless, who hid his death inside a needle, inside an egg, inside a duck, inside a hare, locked in a chest beneath an oak. A lich lord has done the same with his soul and has had centuries to improve the hiding place. What walks the halls is a robed skeleton with a scholar's patience and a touch that stops the limbs.

corrupted_treant.name: corrupted treant
corrupted_treant.lore: Once a shepherd of the forest, slow to anger and older than the kingdoms above. Something poisoned the water at its roots, and the rot went up through the heartwood into its thinking. Its bark has gone black and hard, and its roots grope under the flagstones for ankles. Clubs and arrows barely mark it. An axe does, and fire does better.

skeleton_horde.name: skeleton horde
skeleton_horde.lore: Dozens of the dead from one lost battle, risen together and still keeping formation. They advance shoulder to shoulder, a rattling wall of rust and bone, and the rear ranks throw the splintered ribs of the fallen over the heads of the front. Arrows pass between their ribs. A heavy mace does not, and neither does a prayer.

spectral_dragon.name: spectral dragon
spectral_dragon.lore: When a dragon dies on its hoard and will not let it go, the fury sometimes stays after the flesh is gone. What remains is a pale outline of wings and jaws with cold fire behind the ribs. Its breath does not scorch skin. It burns the part of a man that hopes, and its claws pass through a shield as if through mist.

demon_captain.name: demon captain
demon_captain.lore: An officer of the lower hosts, risen through the ranks by outliving its superiors and arranging the deaths of a few. It carries a blade forged in the pit and still hot from it, and it fights like a veteran: no wasted motion, no pride. Lesser fiends obey it out of fear. It obeys its own masters for the same reason.

iron_sentinel.name: iron sentinel
iron_sentinel.lore: Dwarven smiths built these to stand at vault doors and never ask for wages. Inside the iron shell, gears as fine as a watchmaker's turn on a core that has not run down in a thousand years. The dwarves who held the passwords are dust. The sentinel still asks for them, in a voice like a hinge, and treats silence as a wrong answer.

ancient_vampire_lord.name: ancient vampire lord
ancient_vampire_lord.lore: The Greeks feared the lamia and the Romans the strix, night creatures that drank the blood of the sleeping, long before anyone used the word vampire. This lord claims to remember both names being coined. It has ruled its hunting ground since before the first chronicle, and it regards crusaders the way a landowner regards poachers: a nuisance to be dealt with personally.

elder_storm_giant.name: elder storm giant
elder_storm_giant.lore: The eldest of the storm giants kept halls above the clouds and settled their quarrels with thunder. This one came down long ago, for reasons it does not share. Lightning crawls over its skin like St. Elmo's fire on a ship's mast, and its hammer carries the whole charge. When it claps its hands, the blast alone can knock a knight flat.

primordial_fire_elemental.name: primordial fire elemental
primordial_fire_elemental.lore: Heraclitus of Ephesus taught that the world is an ever-living fire, kindled in measure and quenched in measure. This is some of the unquenched part. It has burned since before there were hearths to hold it, white at the core and loud as a furnace. Stone glows where it passes, and anything that can catch, does. Deep cold is the one thing that makes it flinch.

primordial_ice_elemental.name: primordial ice elemental
primordial_ice_elemental.lore: Norse poets said that before earth or sky there was Niflheim, a world of mist and ice, and that its frozen rivers met the sparks of Muspelheim in the great gap between. This is a piece of that first cold which never thawed. Breath freezes in the air around it. Torches gutter, armor grows brittle, and a careless hand locks to its own sword hilt.

demon_general.name: demon general
demon_general.lore: A commander of legions, one step below the princes of the pit. It has directed sieges that lasted longer than most kingdoms, and it studies an opponent before it kills him, out of professional habit. Its blade burns, its touch rots, and a word from it sends lesser fiends forward to die. It expects to be obeyed and has rarely been surprised.

zombie_legion.name: zombie legion
zombie_legion.lore: Haitian tradition gave the world the zombie: a body raised by a sorcerer and worked without rest or will. A necromancer here has raised a whole graveyard at once and yoked it to a single command. The dead come on in a slow press, packed too tightly to fall, and what they cannot claw they bury under their own weight. Fire clears them. Little else does.

dracolich.name: dracolich
dracolich.lore: A dragon lives a thousand years and still fears the end of them. This one bargained with necromancers, drank what they brewed, and bound its soul into a hidden vessel while the flesh fell away. The bones kept the cunning and the hoard. Its breath is no longer flame but a grey killing mist, and it has all the time in the world to use it.

mythic_hydra.name: mythic hydra
mythic_hydra.lore: The Hydra of Lerna grew two heads for every one Heracles struck off, until his nephew Iolaus seared each stump with a burning brand. The last head could not die at all, so Heracles buried it under a rock by the road. This beast is of that blood and has had centuries to grow. Its heads strike from every side, and one of them spits acid.

corrupted_angel.name: corrupted angel
corrupted_angel.lore: Revelation says the dragon's tail swept a third of the stars from heaven and cast them down. This was one of them. It kept its sword and its soldier's training, and the light that once came from it has soured into a glare that blinds. It remembers what it was. That memory is the cruelest thing about it, and it shares it freely.

titan.name: titan
titan.lore: The Titans ruled before the Olympians. Zeus and his brothers fought them for ten years, and when the thunderbolts finally told, Zeus chained the losers in Tartarus, as far below the earth as the earth is below the sky. Hesiod says a bronze anvil would fall nine days to reach it. The dungeon has dug deep enough to find one. It has not forgotten lightning.

shadow_assassin.name: shadow assassin
shadow_assassin.lore: The Old Man of the Mountain sent his killers out from Alamut with a dagger each, and princes slept badly for two centuries. This order learned the same trade and then went further, bargaining its own shadows away for the right to walk inside them. Nothing is seen until the blade arrives. Bright flame and holy light leave them nowhere to stand.

plague_ooze.name: plague ooze
plague_ooze.lore: Where plague pits drain into the dungeon's lower water, something has gathered itself out of the runoff. It is the color of a bruise and moves like spilled oil against the slope. Metal pits and leather rots at its touch, and those it brushes sicken within the hour. It has no eyes and no malice, only appetite. Fire dries it; frost cracks it.

abyssal_behemoth.name: abyssal behemoth
abyssal_behemoth.lore: The Book of Job describes Behemoth with bones like bars of iron and a tail that sways like a cedar. The pit bred its own answer to that beast and put it to work breaking walls. It is the size of a gatehouse, plated in scorched hide, and it breathes fire hot enough to slag mortar. Armies have routed at the sound of its tread.

arch_lich.name: arch-lich
arch_lich.lore: Few sorcerers manage the rite that makes a lich. Fewer last long enough afterward to grow bored with it. The arch-lich has spent uncounted centuries refining a single art, and has scattered the vessels of its soul so widely that it no longer remembers them all. Spells break against it. Its gaze unmakes, its touch stops the limbs, and it considers visitors an interruption.

elder_dracolich.name: elder dracolich
elder_dracolich.lore: The oldest of the dead dragons, a cathedral of black bone with witchlight in the sockets. It was ancient when it gave up its flesh and has been dead far longer than it lived. Lesser undead gather to it as courtiers to a king. Its breath is a darkness that leaves a curse on whatever survives it, and its tail can bring down a vaulted roof.

primordial_titan.name: primordial titan
primordial_titan.lore: Hesiod wrote that first of all came Chaos, and then broad-breasted Earth, and that Earth's first children were so monstrous their own father Ouranos hid them away in her depths. This is one of that first brood, older than Kronos and never given a name. It is shaped only roughly like a man. When it stamps, the stone rings for a mile.

void_wyrm.name: void wyrm
void_wyrm.lore: A dragon that flew too far into the dark between the stars and came back with some of it. Its scales show no color, only an absence the eye slides off. What it breathes is not fire but a tearing wrongness that leaves men seeing things that are not there. Its bite takes strength rather than flesh. Lightning and holy light still find it solid.

infernal_lord.name: infernal lord
infernal_lord.lore: A lord of the pit holds his fief the way a baron does, by oath, tribute and terror, and answers only to the princes. This one has ruled for ages over a province of the damned and came up to see the war for himself. He carries a greatsword wreathed in hellfire and wears his cruelty like a signet. He does not hurry.

celestial_guardian.name: celestial guardian
celestial_guardian.lore: Genesis says that God placed cherubim and a flaming sword east of Eden to guard the way to the tree of life. Guardians of that kind stand at the deepest vaults here. They are not fallen and they bear no malice. Their charge is to bar the way, and they will weigh a crusader's worth with the blade as readily as anyone's.

entropy_elemental.name: entropy elemental
entropy_elemental.lore: Everything runs down: fires cool, iron rusts, mountains wear into sand. Here that slow law has taken a shape and learned to hurry. It looks like a patch of grey static in the air, and what it touches ages a century in a breath. Blades pit, straps crumble, and a strong arm turns frail. It does not hate. It only finishes things early.

dread_knight_legion.name: dread knight legion
dread_knight_legion.lore: A whole company of oathbreakers, damned together and still under discipline. They ride in a wedge on horses of bone, lances level, and the air ahead of them goes cold enough to wither grass. In life they broke a charge of the faithful. In death they repeat it, night after night, against anyone who enters their ground. Holy water and fire scatter the line.

abyssal_dragon.name: abyssal dragon
abyssal_dragon.lore: Hatched in the pit from a stolen clutch and reared on brimstone. It has a dragon's size and greed and a demon's delight in suffering, and its hide is the color of cooled slag. The fire it breathes is hellfire, its claws are long as scythes, and its bite festers. Saint George would know the shape. He would not like the smell.

flesh_colossus.name: flesh colossus
flesh_colossus.lore: A necromancer who ran short of patience stitched a battlefield into one body. It stands three men high, a patchwork of a thousand soldiers with a dozen faces sunk in its shoulders. It mends itself with whatever it kills, pressing the new flesh in like clay. Lightning made it move in the first place and will just as readily stop it.

locust_swarmlord.name: locust swarmlord
locust_swarmlord.lore: John saw them rise from the smoke of the bottomless pit: locusts shaped like horses armed for battle, with faces like men, teeth like lions, and wings that roared like chariots. Their king is the angel of the abyss, Abaddon. This is one of his captains. Its jaws ring like a gong when it calls the swarm, and the swarm always comes.

pit_executioner.name: pit executioner
pit_executioner.lore: Abaddon's headsmen. In life they were judges who sold their verdicts to kings, and the pit gave them the work they had earned. The hood is riveted on and the cleaver is never set down. They do not read a sentence before carrying it out. They believe, with some reason, that everyone brought before them is guilty of something.

void_seraph.name: void seraph
void_seraph.lore: Isaiah saw the seraphim above the throne, each with six wings: two to cover the face, two to cover the feet, and two to fly. This one fell and kept the wings. When it lowers the upper pair there is nothing behind them, only a hollow where a face and a name used to be. Its gaze unmakes strength, and its voice is the hush of a star going out.

apocalypse_herald.name: apocalypse herald
apocalypse_herald.lore: Seven angels sound seven trumpets in the Revelation of John, and each blast brings a ruin on the earth. This creature stole the idea and none of the authority. The horn has grown into its chest, so that every breath is a blast, and it carries a sickle for the harvest it keeps announcing. Men who hear it believe the end has come, and run.

wormwood_blight.name: wormwood blight
wormwood_blight.lore: At the third trumpet a great star fell burning on the rivers and springs. John gives its name as Wormwood, and writes that a third of the waters turned bitter and many died of drinking them. This is what grew where the star's ash settled: a pale, spreading thing that drinks light and breathes out bile. Its spores poison whatever they touch.

iron_horseman.name: iron horseman
iron_horseman.lore: John saw four riders: one on a white horse, one on red, one on black, and Death on a pale horse with Hades following after. This is none of the four. It is the kind of thing that rides in their dust, armor welded shut, rider and mount grown into one iron shape. It charges with a leveled lance and does not turn aside.

orc_archer.name: orc archer
orc_archer.lore: Orc archers carry shortbows of yew and gut, fletched with crow feathers stained black by kennel smoke. The warband picks them from its runts: too weak for the front line, but patient enough to hold a draw. An archer who hits a clergyman at sixty paces earns an extra hide for the winter.

orc_priest.name: orc priest
orc_priest.lore: Orc clergy serve no single god. They invoke whichever spirit answers loudest. This one bound a battlefield ghost into the haft of his club, and the ghost screams whenever blood is spilled. The other orcs find the sound comforting, and march to it.

orc_marauder.name: orc marauder
orc_marauder.lore: Marauders are the orcs a chieftain lends out for raiding caravans and outlying farms. They train by sprinting downhill in full armor, which teaches the only lesson they need: once the charge has begun, stopping is a worse death than whatever waits at the bottom. They carry boarding axes and shields set with spikes.

orc_warbringer.name: orc warbringer
orc_warbringer.lore: The warbringer carries the warband's banner, a long pole hung with the bones of cousins who disappointed him, and a great curling horn taken from a southern aurochs. The horn carries through stone. An unlucky party hears it several corridors before seeing who blew it, and by then the warband is already running toward the sound.

dread_orc_champion.name: dread orc champion
dread_orc_champion.lore: The dread tribes that hold the deep tunnels choose a champion by single combat, then chain him to the tribal standard until a successor kills him. His armor is patched with breastplates taken from the men he has beaten. By the time the patches outnumber the original plates, he no longer remembers the name his mother gave him.

goblin_sniper.name: goblin sniper
goblin_sniper.lore: Goblin snipers nest in chimneys and ceiling cracks with crossbows balanced on their knees. A sniper will hold his shot if the target stands too near a kinsman. This is not caution. Goblin tradition says a bolt that kills a cousin makes the bolt-mother weep for a season, and nobody wants that on his conscience.

goblin_warpriest.name: goblin warpriest
goblin_warpriest.lore: Goblin warpriests preach one commandment above all others: goblins shall not eat each other for three days after a feast. Enforcing it takes most of their energy. They swing brass censers full of smoldering kobold hair, chant in counting-rhyme so the congregation can follow, and blind the enemy with the smoke when the sermon fails.

hobgoblin_marshal.name: hobgoblin marshal
hobgoblin_marshal.lore: Hobgoblin marshals run their cohorts on strict drill. They are the only goblin-kin who keep ranks, dress their lines and hold under pressure: the discipline of a Roman legion, seen in a cracked iron mirror. A bellowed order from a marshal can stop a knight mid-stride. A marshal's death undoes years of training in a single howling minute.

goblin_kingslayer.name: goblin kingslayer
goblin_kingslayer.lore: Once in a long generation a goblin clutch produces a runt that survives by being smarter and more patient than the rest. The kingslayer kills rulers for a living. Kobold pretenders pay him in captives, hobgoblin generals in steel. He poisons his shortsword, never works without two cousins nearby, and has never yet been hired twice by the same throne.

skeleton_necromancer.name: skeleton necromancer
skeleton_necromancer.lore: A necromancer who outlived his apprentices and then his own body. He kept the trick of binding spirits to bone but lost the trick of speech. The calls he makes to his servants now come out as a clattering of teeth in the wrong order. The servants understand him anyway.

bone_collector.name: bone collector
bone_collector.lore: A patchwork thing built from the bones of every adventurer who failed in this stretch of dungeon, a few centuries' worth, laced together with rawhide and dried tendon. Each rib remembers a different chest, and the result seems to breathe in seventeen rhythms at once. It is always looking for one more piece.

skeleton_lich.name: skeleton lich
skeleton_lich.lore: Not a true lich. A true lich keeps its soul in a hidden vessel, and this one's vessel cracked centuries ago. What remains is the habit of necromancy, performed by a skeleton that no longer remembers why. The summoning still works. The cold still bites.

banshee_lich.name: banshee lich
banshee_lich.lore: In Irish belief the bean sidhe, the woman of the fairy mound, keens outside a house when one of its family is about to die. This one came to mourn a dark wizard and was bound by accident into his bones. Now a lich's craft runs on a banshee's grief. Her wail carries every warning she failed to give, and few hear it three times.

kobold_trapsetter.name: kobold trapsetter
kobold_trapsetter.lore: German miners blamed the kobold for cave-ins, foul air and ore that poisoned the smelter, and named the metal cobalt after him. The warren's trapsetters keep the tradition alive. They favor wounds that bleed slowly, a nicked hamstring or a dart in the forearm, so that a fleeing adventurer collapses far from his friends.

kobold_dragonshield.name: kobold dragonshield
kobold_dragonshield.lore: A dragonshield wears overlapping plates scavenged from the belly of a dead red dragon. They are heavy enough that he can barely run and thick enough that he does not need to. He plants himself in the corridor mouth while the warren's archers shoot past his ears, and he takes great pride in never having ducked.

kobold_pack_leader.name: kobold pack leader
kobold_pack_leader.lore: A pack leader is the warren's oldest survivor: too clever to die early, too small to be worth challenging. He carries a brass whistle on a thong. One short blast means hide, two means rush, and three means abandon the warren and start again somewhere downhill. He has blown three only once.

gnoll_archer.name: gnoll archer
gnoll_archer.lore: Old bestiaries claimed the hyena could mimic a human voice and call a man out of his house by name. Gnoll archers have the laugh and none of the subtlety. Their longbows are stolen from elves, their arrows fletched with hyena down, and they shoot to cripple, because the pack prefers its prey to walk the last mile itself.

gnoll_fang_of_yeenoghu.name: gnoll fang of Yeenoghu
gnoll_fang_of_yeenoghu.lore: Yeenoghu, the Beast of Butchery, marks his most savage worshippers with a hairline of red across the brow, the sign of the fang. A fang does not retreat from a fight, ever. Gnolls say that one who runs will lose his teeth one by one over the following months, and none has cared to test it.

gnoll_alpha_of_yeenoghu.name: gnoll alpha of Yeenoghu
gnoll_alpha_of_yeenoghu.lore: The alpha is the gnoll who survived eating the demon-tainted flesh of the alpha before him. He stands a foot taller than his kin, walks on the knuckles of one hand, and speaks the tongue of the pit in a child's voice. His axe is the thighbone of a stone giant, banded with iron from the cage that once held him.

bandit_thug.name: bandit thug
bandit_thug.lore: The muscle of the gang: usually a farmhand whose lord rode to war and never came back, or a town drunk who learned that travelers cannot call the watch. Alone he is a coward. With a kinsman at his shoulder he will fight to the last shilling.

bandit_archer.name: bandit archer
bandit_archer.lore: Former poachers, and often the most useful members of a roadside gang: quiet, patient, and willing to spend a whole afternoon up a tree. They will not shoot a child or a priest. This is not conscience. Their grandmothers warned them how those debts get collected.

bandit_thief.name: bandit thief
bandit_thief.lore: Thieves drift in and out of bandit work as the seasons demand: winter in a warm gang, spring picking pockets in a market town. They prefer a quiet boot and a turned back to a duel, and they have a saying: the man who shows his sword has already decided he would rather not use it.

bandit_kingpin.name: bandit kingpin
bandit_kingpin.lore: A kingpin holds his stretch of road the way a baron holds a fief: protection paid, debts collected, rivals removed quietly. Some were officers cashiered for treason, some were roadside preachers whose sermons soured. All of them can read, write and count, and that alone is why they lead.

cult_initiate.name: cult initiate
cult_initiate.lore: Initiates are mostly townspeople who took the wrong cup at the wrong vigil. After a year of the cult's catechism they cannot recall the names of their own children. The robe is hemp and the dagger is brass. The conviction is borrowed, but it cuts the same.

cult_priest.name: cult priest
cult_priest.lore: The second tier: initiates who have presided over enough dark rites that they no longer dream about them. They keep the cult's true name secret even from their own kin. Asked what they believe, they quote scripture they do not hold to and watch the questioner's face for the answer.

cult_zealot.name: cult zealot
cult_zealot.lore: A zealot has crossed what the cult calls the third veil, where pain stops registering and conviction takes over. He carries his cleaver in a two-handed grip even at table, and he walks with the rolling gait of a man whose ribs have broken and knit too many times to count.

cult_hierophant.name: cult hierophant
cult_hierophant.lore: The hierophant is the cult's living memory, the only one who knows where the founder is buried and what was buried with her. He no longer eats with his initiates and conducts the great rites alone. When he summons his lessers to die for him, he calls them by their childhood names.

ghast_eater.name: ghast eater
ghast_eater.lore: The ghoul comes from Arabian tales, where the ghul haunts graveyards and desert roads and feeds on the dead. A ghast is what a ghoul becomes when it has also eaten enough of its own kind. Its claws numb a limb at a scratch, and its stench is so foul that other undead give it the corridor.

draugr_wight.name: draugr wight
draugr_wight.lore: The sagas call him a draugr: a barrow-king who would not lie still. Grettir the Strong broke into such a mound, wrestled its dead lord Kar the Old among the grave goods, and cut off his head. This one still holds the sword he was buried with, and his touch takes the warmth from a body and gives it to the barrow.

grave_knight.name: grave knight
grave_knight.lore: A knight who died with an oath unfulfilled and would not let the matter rest. He wakes when his cause is spoken aloud within a mile of his cairn. The oath itself is sometimes petty, a stolen horse or an unpaid wager, but the obligation does not care about size.

greater_imp.name: greater imp
greater_imp.lore: A greater imp is what becomes of an imp that lasts ten years in the mortal world without being killed or banished. The tail thickens, the wings harden, and the creature picks up the vocabulary of a third-rate ambassador. Some keep faith with an old contract. Most do not.

demonic_imp.name: demonic imp
demonic_imp.lore: These no longer pretend to be anyone's familiar. They are the courier class of a small infernal house, sent up to settle scores their betters cannot be bothered with. The sting now carries true hellfire, and the talons are sharp enough to sign a contract on any surface that comes to hand.

imp_lord.name: imp lord
imp_lord.lore: A minor noble of a minor infernal court, somewhere between a baronet and a bookkeeper. He has earned the right to call up other imps for the unpleasant parts of his work, and the right to refuse a duel by pleading higher business elsewhere. He uses both rights freely.

snake_charmer.name: snake charmer
snake_charmer.lore: A cobra is nearly deaf to music. It rises to the sway of the pipe, not the tune, and every charmer knows it. This one learned the trade in the bazaars of Samarkand and went underground when the caravans stopped coming. His drone is meant for human ears, and it sets them hearing and seeing things. His basket is never empty.

viper_priestess.name: viper priestess
viper_priestess.lore: In the ruins of Knossos, Arthur Evans dug up small figures of a woman holding a snake in each raised hand. No one knows her name. The viper priestesses say they do. They serve a snake goddess older than the cities she once guarded, their eyes rarely blink, and they tend their own wounded with a venom bred over centuries to heal kin instead of killing.

cave_troll.name: Cave Troll
cave_troll.lore: In the Norse tales a troll caught above ground at sunrise turns to stone, which is why the breed keeps to caves. This one has never seen the sun and does not intend to. It has long arms for close work and a ridged hide that shrugs off clubs. Its wounds knit while the fight is still going. Burns and acid scars do not.

harrow_witch.name: Harrow Witch
harrow_witch.lore: She came down from the heath when the kingdoms above forgot to fear her, and she has worked the lower halls ever since. There are bones braided in her hair and old curses on her tongue. Her touch brings the rot and her hexes sap the strength from a sword arm. Wise men settle with her from a distance.

moss_sentinel.name: Moss Sentinel
moss_sentinel.lore: Carved as a boundary marker on some forgotten threshold, then forgotten itself, until the moss crept over it and gave it a body. It stands where it was set and waits. When something comes near, the moss remembers what the stone was for. Arrows and hammers find little to hurt. A sharp edge strips the green away, and fire does it faster.

sable_serpent.name: Sable Serpent
sable_serpent.lore: Black as wet coal and silent over stone. The country folk called them sable serpents and would not name them after dark. Like any snake, it grows sluggish in the cold and seeks out warm places, which in a dungeon means the living. Its venom works slowly, and that is the only mercy in the encounter.

iron_patriarch.name: The Iron Patriarch
iron_patriarch.lore: He was father to a line of tyrants and he outlived every one of them. Sons, grandsons and usurpers went into the family crypt while he sat on, sealed in the plate he wore to his coronation, until the kingdom itself gave out beneath him. The dungeon found him still expecting an audience. His guards still answer his call. He grants each visitor a hearing, and it is short, and it ends with the hammer. Blades skate off the old plate. Lightning finds the man inside it.
iron_patriarch.omen: Someone has kept this floor swept and the torches trimmed, as for a court.
iron_patriarch.enrage_message: The Iron Patriarch rises from his throne. The audience is over.
rage_messages: The Iron Patriarch remembers how he took the crown.
The Iron Patriarch fights like a man who has outlived every heir.

mage_slayer_assassin.name: Mage-Slayer Assassin
mage_slayer_assassin.lore: An order raised inside the wizards' towers to hunt renegades, then turned against the towers themselves. Each slayer wears wards sewn into the lining of the coat, so spells slide off. The first cut goes for the casting hand and the second for the throat, to stop the voice. The rest of the work, they say, is bookkeeping.

stone_golem.name: Stone Golem
stone_golem.lore: The masons built it to guard the lower stair, and then the masons died. It still guards the lower stair. There is no spark of thought behind its face, only one instruction cut too deep to wear away. Swords chip and arrows skip off the granite. A miner's hammer or a flask of acid gets further.

plague_witch.name: Plague Witch
plague_witch.lore: During the Black Death, frightened towns blamed witches and well-poisoners for the sickness. This woman would have deserved it. She gathers the dying at the gate and brings them down with her; they serve her, and her craft keeps them on their feet. She wears a green hood. When she falls, everything she was holding up falls with her.

vine_horror.name: Vine Horror
vine_horror.lore: It grows where blood was spilled and no one came to bury the dead. It looks like a heap of dry creeper on the wall until something warm passes underneath. Then the tendrils drop and tighten, and the thorns go to work. Cold does not kill it and arrows pass through the tangle. It must be cut at root and stem, or burned.

lurking_horror.name: Lurking Horror
lurking_horror.lore: The greater cousin of the petty mimic, schooled in patience and in chests. It can hold the shape of a locked coffer for years without a twitch. Adventurers find it exactly where they most hope to find the thing it is pretending to be. The lid is a mouth, the hinges are teeth, and the lock was never locked.

ettin_warchief.name: Ettin Warchief
ettin_warchief.lore: Two heads on one pair of shoulders, and they disagreed about everything for forty years. Together they led their clan to ruin, each blaming the other for the route. The dungeon keeps what is left. The right head gives orders and the left one countermands them, yet both clubs somehow land on the same target.

throne_sentinel.name: Throne Sentinel
throne_sentinel.lore: A suit of armor cast for a king's bodyguard, given motion by court enchanters and never stood down. The smithwork is finer than any living foundry can copy. It guards an empty throne with halberd and shield, and it still salutes an opponent who lands a clean blow before it answers in kind.

whispering_crone.name: The Whispering Crone
whispering_crone.lore: She told fortunes in a market town and told them too plainly: which child would not see spring, which husband would not come home. The town buried her alive for it. In the dark of the grave she went on whispering, and after some years things began to whisper back. Now specters and wraiths come at her call like hounds to a huntsman. Her voice carries no farther than a breath, yet every listener hears his own death foretold in it, with the day and the hour. She has not been wrong yet.
whispering_crone.omen: A voice starts in as soon as you arrive, low and close. It knows your name.
rage_messages: The Whispering Crone speaks a name, and it is yours.
The Whispering Crone's friends press closer in the dark.

demonic_trickster.name: Demonic Trickster
demonic_trickster.lore: Hell sends its clever ones up to negotiate, and they never do. This one prefers the moment just before: the open hand, the reasonable smile, and then a blade of warped fire arriving from an angle that should not exist. It mocks as it fights, and its victims end up striking at the laughter instead of the demon.

deep_one_priest.name: Deep-One Priest
deep_one_priest.lore: Certain villages on the coast bred a strain that could almost pass for human: wide eyes, flat noses, a shuffle in the walk. When the wells went dry their priests climbed down them and kept going. They pray to something under the sea in a tongue full of water. The prayer keeps their flock standing long after it should have fallen.

gilded_mimic.name: Gilded Mimic
gilded_mimic.lore: Old enough to have learned what adventurers really look for. It no longer bothers with a single chest. It spreads itself as a king's hoard, spilled open as if some other party had already won the fight and left in a hurry. Even the false coins have real gold in them, which makes the disguise expensive and very reliable.

frostfang_giant.name: Frostfang Giant
frostfang_giant.lore: The frost giants of Norse song kept their halls in Jotunheim, beyond a river that never freezes. Frostfangs are the kin they cast out. They came down into the deeps looking for warmth and found a different cold instead, and it suited them. They carry mauls of glacier ice, breathe a numbing fog, and remember the slight.

crypt_summoner.name: Crypt Summoner
crypt_summoner.lore: A graduate of a school the surface has forgotten, and dead himself for longer than he studied. He treats necromancy as plain bookkeeping: which corpse, which name, what wage is owed. He has kept those books for a very long time, and they balance. Any stranger who enters his crypt is entered in the ledger at once, as an asset.

shadow_archer.name: Shadow Archer
shadow_archer.lore: Trained in towers that appear on no map. The first lesson is the bow. The second is to stop being where the arrow came from. The masters keep the third lesson to themselves. Their arrows are fletched with darkness and leave the eyes dim. Firelight and holy light give them nowhere to hide.

veiled_inquisitor.name: Veiled Inquisitor
veiled_inquisitor.lore: Sent long ago by an authority that no longer exists, to find heretics who no longer remember the doctrine. He has improvised. The scourge is real, the burning censer is real, and the creed is whatever he last said it was. He hides his face behind a veil. No true servant of the Church ever needed to.

lava_elemental.name: Lava Elemental
lava_elemental.lore: Where the dungeon presses against a vein of magma, the fire sometimes forgets to be only fire, and gets up. It wears a crust of black rock that cracks orange at every step. Arrows melt in it and hammers sink. It has no idea what walking is for, but it has grown very good at what comes after walking up to someone.

blood_archon.name: Blood Archon
blood_archon.lore: An older grade of fiend, from the days when bargains were written in blood and signed in the same. He keeps a ledger bound in something that was never calfskin. The column of debts is long, the column of repayments is short, and the interest is what it has always been. Kings signed with him for victories and merchants for fair winds, and he has collected from every one. He fights the way he trades, opening a vein and waiting. Steel only feeds the account. Fire and a blessing cancel it.
blood_archon.omen: A ledger lies open on the stair. The last entry is your name, with the amount left blank.
blood_archon.enrage_message: The Blood Archon closes his ledger.
rage_messages: The Blood Archon adds the interest.

astral_horror.name: Astral Horror
astral_horror.lore: It came through a door that someone left open in a dream, and it has not yet decided whether to leave. It has no fixed outline, only a suggestion of eyes and reaching thought. Minds near it grow muddled and strength drains away like water from a cracked jug. It appears to be curious. Its curiosity is rarely survived.

tiamat.name: Tiamat the Five-Headed Dragon Queen
tiamat.lore: In the Babylonian Enuma Elish, Tiamat is the salt sea, mother of the first gods and of the monsters she raised against them. The young god Marduk drove the winds into her open jaws, shot an arrow down her throat, and split her body in two to make the sky and the earth. Later storytellers gave her five dragon heads and named her queen of evil dragonkind. That is the shape that wakes beneath the dungeon: five crowned heads, each breathing a different ruin, frost, flame, lightning, acid and venom, and behind them the oldest grudge in the world.
tiamat.omen: The air tastes of salt, and the stone is wet with something that is not water.

asmodeus.name: Asmodeus, Prince of Hell
asmodeus.lore: The Book of Tobit names Asmodeus as the demon who killed seven husbands of Sarah, each on his wedding night. On the advice of the angel Raphael, young Tobias burned the heart and liver of a fish, and the smoke drove the demon to the far reaches of Egypt, where Raphael bound him. Later tradition made him a prince of Hell who rules by contract instead of fury. Every soul he owns signed its own surrender, and the ruby rod in his hand seals each bargain. He has not forgiven the fish.
asmodeus.omen: Somewhere on this floor a table is laid for two, and a bell is rung for dinner.

surtur.name: Surtur the Fire Giant Lord
surtur.lore: Surtur, whom the Norse poets called Surt, stands guard at the border of Muspelheim, the realm of fire, with a sword that outshines the sun. The Voluspa foretells that at Ragnarok he will ride from the south with flame before and behind him, cut down the god Freyr, and cast fire over the whole earth until it sinks into the sea. He has not yet been called to that battle. Until the horn sounds he waits below, and the stone around him runs like wax. Cold is the one thing a lord of fire has reason to respect.
surtur.omen: The stone here is warm and runs like wax.

ymir_last_spawn.name: Ymir's Last Spawn
ymir_last_spawn.lore: Ymir was the first of the frost giants, born where the ice of Niflheim met the sparks of Muspelheim. Odin and his brothers Vili and Ve killed him and built the world from the corpse: his flesh the soil, his blood the sea, his bones the mountains, his skull the dome of the sky. The blood drowned all his kin but Bergelmir and his wife. This giant claims descent from neither. It says it was there before the flood, and it carries the cold of that first morning in its breath.
ymir_last_spawn.omen: Frost has grown on the inside of the walls.

hrungnirs_ghost.name: Hrungnir's Ghost
hrungnirs_ghost.lore: Hrungnir was the strongest of the giants, with a heart of hard stone, sharp-edged and three-cornered, and a head and shield of stone to match. Drunk in Asgard, he boasted he would carry Valhalla home, and Thor met him in a duel at the border. The giant threw his whetstone and Thor threw Mjolnir. The hammer broke the whetstone in the air and then broke Hrungnir's skull, and a splinter of the stone stayed lodged in Thor's head ever after. The ghost still walks, still hurling shards, still demanding a rematch.
hrungnirs_ghost.omen: Chips of whetstone are scattered across the floor, as if thrown.

bonnacon.name: Bonnacon
bonnacon.lore: The bestiaries place the bonnacon in Paeonia and give it a bull's body and a horse's mane. Its horns curl so far back on themselves that they cannot hurt anyone, which Pliny noted with some sympathy. It has another defence. It runs, and as it runs it sprays dung across the ground behind it, and whatever the dung touches burns as if set alight. Monks painted this in the margins of their books for three hundred years, and the knight in the picture always looks as if he regrets his career.
bonnacon.omen: The floor ahead is scorched in long streaks, and smells worse than it looks.

calydonian_boar.name: Calydonian Boar
calydonian_boar.lore: King Oeneus of Calydon gave first fruits to every god at harvest and forgot Artemis. She sent a boar. Ovid says it was bigger than a bull, with bristles like spear shafts and tusks like an elephant's, and that it trampled the vines and the corn alike. Half the heroes of Greece came to hunt it. Atalanta's arrow drew first blood, Meleager's spear ended it, and the quarrel over who should keep the hide killed more of them than the boar had.
calydonian_boar.omen: The corridors here are ploughed up as if by a harrow, stone and all.
